Agli eredi della tenuta, prima che decid.easy: To the heirs of the estate, before they make their choice.
Agli eredi della tenuta, prima che decid.short: To the heirs of the estate, before they decide.

Vi mando il Registro della mia famiglia:.easy: I am sending you my family's Register. It is three notebooks with black cloth covers. Inside are fifty-four years of births, fevers, broken bones and temperatures. My grandmother Hester began it. She was a midwife, and nobody let her call herself a doctor. My father Joost went on with it. He was a real doctor, but he never believed in it. Now I am finishing it. I spent four years in the war, and now I believe almost anything.
Vi mando il Registro della mia famiglia:.short: I am sending you my family's Register: fifty-four years of births, fevers and temperatures, begun by my grandmother Hester, kept by my father Joost, closed by me.

Non vi chiedo di credermi. Vi chiedo di.easy: I do not ask you to believe me. I ask you to count. Count the temperatures that are too low. Count the people who get better too quickly. Count the names that appear twice. Count the people of the village who do not dream any more. Then decide.
Non vi chiedo di credermi. Vi chiedo di.short: Do not believe me: count. The cold temperatures, the quick recoveries, the names written twice, the people who no longer dream. Then decide.

Notte, ore undici e un quarto. Di ritorn.easy: Night, a quarter past eleven. I was coming back from the miller's house: his wife had a baby boy, healthy. From the road on the dyke I saw a white light on the tower of the estate. It was as bright as day, with no smoke and no noise. At the same moment, I swear it, there was another light just like it in the middle of the bog, where there is nothing and nobody. Both lights lasted only a breath. Then it was dark.
Notte, ore undici e un quarto. Di ritorn.short: A quarter past eleven at night. From the dyke I saw a white light on the estate's tower, and at the same moment another one in the middle of the empty bog. A breath, then darkness.

Mattina. Medicate le mani di Fokke Tamme.easy: Morning. I put bandages on the hands of Fokke Tammer, who cuts peat. His palms are badly burnt. He says he found a black stone in the water, where the light was. It was as hot as a stove, and he pulled it out. He will not tell me where he has put it.
Mattina. Medicate le mani di Fokke Tamme.short: Morning. Fokke Tammer, peat-cutter, has burnt palms: he pulled a hot black stone out of the water where the light was. He will not say where it is.

Morto stanotte il signore della tenuta,.easy: The master of the estate died last night. It was his heart. They called me too late. In his last days he did not sleep, and he talked a lot, always about the tower. He held my wrist so hard that it hurt. "Something came through," he said. "I do not know what. It must go back where it came from." Pastor Kalf says he was out of his mind. I write his words here because he asked me to, and because nobody else will.
Morto stanotte il signore della tenuta,.short: The master of the estate died last night. At the end he held my wrist: "Something came through. It must go back where it came from." The pastor says he was raving. I write it down anyway.

Da qualche giorno, ogni mattina, la lava.easy: For some days now, every morning, Smit the washerwoman stops at the gate of the estate and waves to you. In thirty years she has never done this. She never says hello to anyone. Last year she even threw a bucket of dirty water at you. Now she smiles, asks how you are, and waits for your answer. She says her hands are red with cold, but she does not put them in her pockets.
Da qualche giorno, ogni mattina, la lava.short: Every morning Smit the washerwoman, who greets nobody, stops at your gate to wave and smile. Her hands are red with cold, but she never puts them in her pockets.

Il vicino nuovo, quello che si è trasfer.easy: The new neighbour moved into the house across the road last spring. Every Sunday they bring you a basket of apples, and every Sunday they ask if you need anything. They mend the roof tiles before anyone asks. They know the names of all your dogs. In the evening they stand at their window, with the lamp off, and look at yours.
Il vicino nuovo, quello che si è trasfer.short: The new neighbour across the road brings apples every Sunday and knows your dogs' names. In the evening they stand at their dark window and watch yours.

Al ritorno dalla città trovi la tua casa.easy: When you come back from town, your house is clean. The windows are washed, and the firewood is cut and stacked. There is a note on the table, in round, friendly handwriting: *We found you a little neglected. Think nothing of it. Your neighbours.* The door was locked. There are only two keys, and you have both of them in your pocket.
Al ritorno dalla città trovi la tua casa.short: Back from town, you find the house cleaned and a note: *We found you a little neglected. Your neighbours.* The door was locked, and both keys are in your pocket.

Ricambi: un saluto, un dolce, un invito.easy: You are kind in return: a greeting, a cake, an invitation to dinner. The neighbour accepts everything, says thank you for everything, and forgets nothing. From that day, in the village, people call your family "decent folk", and the shops let you pay later.
Ricambi: un saluto, un dolce, un invito.short: You return the kindness. From then on your family are "decent folk", and the shops give you credit.

Chiudi le imposte e tiri il chiavistello.easy: You close the shutters and lock the door. The neighbour does not knock, does not call, and is not offended. They stay outside until evening, patient, like someone who knows how to wait. When they finally go away, there is the print of a hand on the window glass, all misty. It stays there for an hour.
Chiudi le imposte e tiri il chiavistello.short: You close the shutters. The neighbour waits outside until evening, patient, and leaves a misty handprint on the glass that lasts an hour.

Ti svegli prima dell'alba con le mani ge.easy: You wake up before dawn with icy hands, as if they had been in water all night. The bed is dry. The room is warm and the fire is lit. But your hands stay cold and damp until midday. When you smell them, they smell of peat smoke.
Ti svegli prima dell'alba con le mani ge.short: You wake with icy, damp hands in a warm, dry bed. They stay cold until noon, and smell of peat smoke.

Stringi la mano a un cliente, e lui la r.easy: You shake hands with a client, and he pulls his hand away fast. "Sorry," he says, "your hands are ice cold." You smile at him. He does not smile back. On the way home you look at your fingers under a street lamp. They are white, clean and still. Too still. They do not shake any more, not even when you are afraid.
Stringi la mano a un cliente, e lui la r.short: A client pulls his hand away: "Your hands are frozen." Under a street lamp your fingers look white and steady. Too steady: they no longer shake even when you are afraid.

Al fronte, i medici dicevano che il fred.easy: At the front, the doctors said that cold feet were the first sign of gangrene. In {0} the cold starts in the hands. This morning you warmed a cup of milk and held it tight until it was completely cold. The milk got cold. Your hands did not get warm.
Al fronte, i medici dicevano che il fred.short: At the front, cold feet meant gangrene. In {0} it starts with the hands: this morning a hot cup of milk went cold in yours, and your hands stayed cold.

Le tieni vicino alla fiamma finché la pe.easy: You hold your hands near the fire until the skin is red and starts to hurt. The pain is good news: it means they are still yours. In the evening, while you write, you notice that you are checking how warm the ink is.
Le tieni vicino alla fiamma finché la pe.short: You hold them to the flame until they hurt: good, they are still yours. That evening you catch yourself checking the temperature of the ink.

Il medico ti mette il termometro sotto i.easy: The doctor puts a thermometer under your arm. He waits, looks at it, and writes a number in the Register. He does not tell you the number. Then he asks if you have drunk water from the bog. You say no. He writes that down too.
Il medico ti mette il termometro sotto i.short: The doctor takes your temperature and writes it in the Register without telling you. He asks if you have drunk bog water. You say no. He writes that down too.

Hai messo sotto la lente un pugno di tor.easy: You put a handful of peat under the lens. It comes from the dyke, where the light was. You see fibres, roots, black seeds and the wing of an insect that died long ago. Then, while you watch, one of the fibres moves. It reaches slowly towards the lamp, like a finger.
Hai messo sotto la lente un pugno di tor.short: Under the lens, the peat from the dyke shows fibres, roots and seeds. Then one fibre moves, and reaches slowly towards the lamp like a finger.

Il microscopio nuovo, quello comprato in.easy: The new microscope, which you bought in the city, makes things three hundred times bigger. In the drop of dark water there are things that no book describes. Thin threads tie and untie themselves, always in the same order. If you watch them long enough, the order looks like a face. Your face.
Il microscopio nuovo, quello comprato in.short: Under the new microscope, threads in the dark water knot and untie in a precise order. Watch long enough, and the order becomes a face. Yours.

Il laboratorio dell'University ti presta.easy: The University laboratory lends you a German machine and an assistant who asks no questions. Under the lens you put a piece of a Neighbour. You took it from the peat in the street where the Neighbour fell apart. The cells are perfect, in neat rows, the same as a person's cells. They are just made of something different.
Il laboratorio dell'University ti presta.short: At the University, under a German lens, a fragment of a crumbled Neighbour shows perfect human cells. They are just made of something else.

Lo studi per giorni, finché non lo conos.easy: You study it for days, until you know it by heart. You learn a lot. And you have a strange, clear feeling that, at the same time, it has learned something about you.
Lo studi per giorni, finché non lo conos.short: You study it for days and learn a great deal. You feel, absurdly, that it has learned something about you too.

Lo bruci nel fornello. Brucia piano, sen.easy: You burn it in the stove. It burns slowly, with no flame, like peat. The smoke smells sweet and stays in the room for a week. But you still remember what you saw.
Lo bruci nel fornello. Brucia piano, sen.short: You burn it. It smoulders like peat, and its sweet smoke stays for a week. You still remember what you saw.

Il sindaco Wessel ti invita al pranzo de.easy: Mayor Wessel invites you to the council lunch, on the first Thursday of the month, and you sit at his right. People talk about peat, dykes and the price of butter. Nobody talks about the two lights. At dessert the mayor raises his glass "to the family of the estate, who will take {0} into the future". Everyone drinks water.
Il sindaco Wessel ti invita al pranzo de.short: At the council lunch Mayor Wessel seats you at his right and toasts your family, "who will carry {0} into the future". Nobody mentions the lights. Everyone drinks water.

Il consiglio ti offre un seggio. Le sedu.easy: The council offers you a seat. The meetings are very short. Nobody argues, nobody says no, and the accounts are right to the last penny. At the end of the first meeting the clerk shakes your hand and says you are "just like them". In {0}, that is a compliment.
Il consiglio ti offre un seggio. Le sedu.short: You join the council. Nobody ever argues, and the accounts balance to the penny. The clerk says you are "just like them". In {0}, that is a compliment.

La città ti nomina presidente del comita.easy: The town makes you the head of the committee for the war memorial. The bronze is already ordered. The names are already chosen. The day of the ceremony is already fixed. They only want your signature and a speech. In the speech, they ask, please say nothing about the bog: "Our boys came home. That is what matters."
La città ti nomina presidente del comita.short: The town puts you in charge of the war memorial: everything is decided, they only want your signature and a speech. Not a word about the bog, please: "Our boys came home."

Accetti, ringrazi, fai quello che ti chi.easy: You accept, you say thank you, and you do what they ask. They welcome you like one of the family, with a warmth that has no cracks. It feels nice. It feels so nice that, on the way home, you have to stop for a moment to remember the question you wanted to ask.
Accetti, ringrazi, fai quello che ti chi.short: You accept. They welcome you like family, so warmly that on the way home you cannot remember what you wanted to ask.

Rifiuti, con tutte le buone maniere che.easy: You say no, as politely as you can. Nobody is offended. In {0} nobody is ever offended now. They smile at you, they thank you anyway, and they watch you go, like a guest who came to the wrong house.
Rifiuti, con tutte le buone maniere che.short: You decline politely. Nobody in {0} takes offence any more: they smile, thank you, and watch you go like a guest at the wrong house.

L'acqua della torbiera è scura come il t.easy: The water of the bog is as dark as tea that has been left too long, and it is cold even in summer. People who have drunk it say it tastes of smoke and earth. They say it clears your head better than coffee. The pastor says it is the devil's water. The pastor only drinks wine.
L'acqua della torbiera è scura come il t.short: The bog water is dark as stewed tea and cold even in summer. They say it clears the head better than coffee. The pastor calls it the devil's water, and drinks wine.

A {0} l'acqua della torbiera si vende in.easy: In {0} they sell the bog water in bottles with a label: "{1} Water, for health and serenity". The chemist says it is good if you cannot sleep. The schoolmistress says it is good if you cannot pay attention. The mayor says it is good for everything else. Nobody in the village has been ill for years.
A {0} l'acqua della torbiera si vende in.short: The bog water is sold in bottles, "{0} Water, for health and serenity", and recommended for everything. Nobody in the village has been ill for years.

Nel bicchiere l'acqua scura non si muove.easy: The dark water in the glass does not move, not even when you hit the table. At the front you drank water from puddles, from snow, even from radiators. This water is different. It is looking at you.
Nel bicchiere l'acqua scura non si muove.short: The dark water in the glass does not move, even when you knock the table. You drank worse at the front. But this water looks back.

Il freddo scende fino allo stomaco e si.easy: The cold goes down into your stomach and spreads slowly, like ink in a glass of water. Then your mind becomes very clear. Your thoughts put themselves in order. Your worries become small and far away. For a few hours you are not afraid of anything. It is the nicest feeling of your life, and that is what frightens you most.
Il freddo scende fino allo stomaco e si.short: The cold spreads through you like ink, and your mind turns clear and calm. For a few hours you fear nothing. That, more than anything, frightens you.

Guardi il tuo riflesso nell'acqua scura,.easy: You look at your reflection in the dark water for a long time. Then you leave the glass where it is. As you walk away, you feel that the reflection is still there, watching you leave.
Guardi il tuo riflesso nell'acqua scura,.short: You stare at your reflection, then leave the glass. Walking away, you feel the reflection is still watching you.

Stamattina, allo specchio, hai dovuto pe.easy: This morning, in the mirror, you needed a moment to know who you were looking at. Only a moment.
Stamattina, allo specchio, hai dovuto pe.short: This morning, in the mirror, it took you a moment to recognise yourself.

Fuori, il paese ti sembra un po' più qui.easy: Outside, the village seems a little quieter than before. Or maybe you are the one who is quieter.
Fuori, il paese ti sembra un po' più qui.short: Outside, the village seems quieter. Or perhaps you are.

Gli prendi la mano davanti a tutti e la.easy: In front of everyone, you take its hand and squeeze it hard, until the skin breaks. No blood comes out of the cut. Dark water comes out, slowly, and it smells of smoke.
Gli prendi la mano davanti a tutti e la.short: You squeeze its hand in front of everyone until the skin splits. Out comes not blood but dark water, smelling of smoke.

Davanti alla gente radunata gli mostri l.easy: In front of the crowd you show it the Evidence, one piece after another: the temperature, the scar that has disappeared, the name that is written twice in the Register. It listens kindly and does not deny anything.
Davanti alla gente radunata gli mostri l.short: Before the crowd you lay out the Evidence: the temperature, the missing scar, the name written twice. It listens kindly, denying nothing.

Wil Maas gli punge il dito con un ago, d.easy: In front of everyone, Wil Maas pricks its finger with a needle. A black drop comes out. The Neighbour looks at the drop, then at you, and smiles like someone caught cheating at cards.
Wil Maas gli punge il dito con un ago, d.short: Wil Maas pricks its finger before everyone: a black drop. The Neighbour smiles like a card cheat caught out.

Il Vicino non scappa e non si difende. S.easy: The Neighbour does not run away and does not fight. It sits on the ground, looks at its hands, and starts to lose its shape, like a statue made of earth in the rain. After a few minutes there is only a pile of wet peat, with a button and a pair of glasses in it. The village watches in silence. Nobody thanks you.
Il Vicino non scappa e non si difende. S.short: The Neighbour sits down and melts like earth in the rain, leaving wet peat, a button and a pair of spectacles. The village watches in silence. Nobody thanks you.

Lasci perdere. Il Vicino ti augura buona.easy: You let it go. The Neighbour wishes you a good day, and really means it.
Lasci perdere. Il Vicino ti augura buona.short: You let it go. The Neighbour wishes you a good day, and means it.

Sepolto oggi il signore della tenuta, ne.easy: Today they buried the master of the estate, in the cemetery on the dyke. It was raining. Only a few people came: his children, Pastor Kalf, the notary from the city and a few curious people. Mayor Wessel sent flowers and said he could not come because of his gout. Fokke Tammer stood at the back with his bandaged hands. He did not take off his hat.
Sepolto oggi il signore della tenuta, ne.short: The master of the estate was buried today, in the rain. Few came. Fokke Tammer stood at the back, hands bandaged, and kept his hat on.

Il signore era un uomo strano, ma pagava.easy: The master was a strange man, but he always paid me on time for the births, and he never called me "the woman". In his last months he spent his nights in the tower. It is a brick building that he had built behind the house, as tall as the church tower. At night, from the dyke, people saw blue flashes at its windows. The village said he was doing alchemy. I said he was just staying up late.
Il signore era un uomo strano, ma pagava.short: The master was strange, but he paid on time. In his last months he spent his nights in his brick tower, where blue flashes lit the windows. The village said alchemy. I said late hours.

Ora la torre è chiusa. La serratura, dic.easy: Now the tower is closed. The smith says the lock has melted, as if someone had welded it from the inside. But nobody is inside, because the only person who lived there is in the coffin we have just put in the ground.
Ora la torre è chiusa. La serratura, dic.short: Now the tower is shut, its lock melted as if welded from inside. Yet its only occupant is in the coffin we just lowered.

Dopo il funerale il notaio ha consegnato.easy: After the funeral the notary gave each child a page from their father's Journal. Each page was torn out and folded, with a name on it. The will said so. At the church door, one of the children showed me their page and asked me if their father was still in his right mind when he wrote it. I told the truth: I do not know.
Dopo il funerale il notaio ha consegnato.short: After the funeral the notary gave each child a folded page of their father's Journal. One asked me if he was still sane when he wrote it. I do not know.

*11 novembre, notte. L'anello si è acces.easy: *11 November, night. The ring turned on by itself. I did not touch it, I swear. I was at the window, and my pipe was out. White light, no heat, a hum like bees inside a wall. Then nothing. I did not send anything, but it turned on anyway. It was made to send things, not to receive them. What has it received?*
*11 novembre, notte. L'anello si è acces.short: *11 November, night. The ring lit up by itself: white light, a hum like bees. I sent nothing. It was made to send, not to receive. What has it received?*

Sotto, un disegno a matita: la torre, l'.easy: Under the words there is a pencil drawing: the tower, the ring at the top, and a dotted line. The line starts at the ring and goes, straight as a thread, to the middle of an area full of little dashes. The bog.
Sotto, un disegno a matita: la torre, l'.short: Below, a pencil drawing: a dotted line runs straight from the ring on the tower into the middle of the bog.

*Tammer non è Tammer. Guardategli le man.easy: *Tammer is not Tammer. Look at his hands. He burnt them that night, and the next day the bandages were dry. He does not drink any more. He does not curse any more. He has cut more peat in one month than in a whole year. He says hello to everyone by name, even to the people he hated. His wife now sleeps at her sister's house.*
*Tammer non è Tammer. Guardategli le man.short: *Tammer is not Tammer. His bandages were dry the day after. He no longer drinks or curses, greets everyone by name. His wife sleeps at her sister's.*

Sotto, più piccolo, sottolineato due vol.easy: Under it, in smaller letters, underlined twice: *He is not wicked. It is worse than that: he is happy.*
Sotto, più piccolo, sottolineato due vol.short: Underlined twice: *He is not wicked. It is worse: he is content.*

*Sul pavimento della torre, la mattina d.easy: *The next morning, on the floor of the tower, I found my watch. But my watch is in my waistcoat pocket. I took it out and held both of them in my hand. They are the same: the same crest, the same scratch on the lid. But the one from the floor is old and worn, and its glass is cracked. As if it had been through a war.*
*Sul pavimento della torre, la mattina d.short: *On the tower floor I found my watch, though mine was in my waistcoat. Identical, scratch and all. But the one from the floor is old and cracked, as if it had been through a war.*

Sotto, con un'altra penna: *L'ho dato al.easy: Under it, written with a different pen: *I gave it to the midwife to pay her. I do not want it in the house.*
Sotto, con un'altra penna: *L'ho dato al.short: In another pen: *I gave it to the midwife. I do not want it in the house.*

*È passato qualcosa. Non so che cosa. No.easy: *Something came through. I do not know what it is. I do not know where it came from. I have done the calculations a hundred times, and they are wrong every time. The Machine was not on, so nobody sent it from here. So who sent it?*
*È passato qualcosa. Non so che cosa. No.short: *Something came through, from I know not where. The Machine was off: nobody sent it from here. Then who?*

*Qualunque cosa sia, non è sua questa te.easy: *Whatever it is, it does not belong in this land. It must go back where it came from. If I cannot send it back, tell my children. Tell my children's children.*
*Qualunque cosa sia, non è sua questa te.short: *Whatever it is, it does not belong here. It must go back. If I fail, tell my children, and theirs.*

Pieghi il foglio in quattro e lo infili.easy: You fold the page in four and put it with your papers. It is yours, after all: your name is on it. You will tell the others what you want, when you want. For now, you think it is only the crazy talk of a lonely old man, shut in a tower, talking to his machines.
Pieghi il foglio in quattro e lo infili.short: You fold the sheet away among your papers. It has your name on it. For now it seems the ravings of a lonely old man in a tower.

La mattina dopo, a colazione, leggi il f.easy: The next morning, at breakfast, you read the page out loud. Someone laughs, then stops. Someone shakes their head: everyone knew that their father was not well in his last months. Someone else says nothing and looks out of the window at the tower.
La mattina dopo, a colazione, leggi il f.short: At breakfast you read it aloud. One laughs, then stops. One shakes their head. One looks out at the tower and says nothing.

La tenuta è una casa lunga e bassa ai ma.easy: The estate is a long, low house at the edge of the village. It has a roof of reeds and windows that look out over the bog. Behind the house is the tower. It is made of red bricks, with no windows on the lower half, and at the top there is a closed room with four big windows. In the morning the crows land on it. They never stay long.
La tenuta è una casa lunga e bassa ai ma.short: The estate is a long, low house facing the bog. Behind it rises the red-brick tower, with a shut glass room at the top. Crows land there in the morning, but never stay.

{0} è un paese di torbai: un centinaio d.easy: {0} is a village of peat-cutters. There are about a hundred wooden houses around the church, a market, a mill, and a dyke that keeps the river out. All around is the bog, flat and dark as far as you can see. In winter it is full of fog, and in summer it is full of mosquitoes. For hundreds of years the people here have cut the peat into bricks, dried it and burnt it. Peat does not give much heat, and it makes a lot of smoke. But it is free, and it belongs to everyone.
{0} è un paese di torbai: un centinaio d.short: {0} is a village of peat-cutters: wooden houses, a church, a mill, a dyke, and the flat dark bog all around. Peat gives little heat and much smoke, but it is free, and everyone's.

A metà mattina qualcuno bussa al cancell.easy: In the middle of the morning someone knocks at the gate. It is Fokke Tammer, the peat-cutter. His hands are bandaged, and he has a wheelbarrow full of bricks of dark peat, almost black. He offers them as a gift, "for the master's family, to show respect". He says this peat is warmer than any other. He says it makes no smoke. And he smiles. Nobody in the village remembers ever seeing him smile.
A metà mattina qualcuno bussa al cancell.short: Fokke Tammer comes to the gate with a barrow of almost black peat, a gift "for the master's family". It makes no smoke, he says. He smiles, and nobody has ever seen him smile.

Fokke entra, si siede in cucina e accett.easy: Fokke comes in, sits in the kitchen and accepts a glass of water, not gin. He talks kindly about the master, about the weather and about peat. The cook lights the fire with his bricks. The flame is low and quiet, and the room gets warm in a few minutes. Fokke never goes near the fire. He keeps his hands in his lap, and when he leaves he says thank you three times.
Fokke entra, si siede in cucina e accett.short: Fokke sits in the kitchen and drinks water, not gin. His peat burns low and silent and warms the room in minutes. He never goes near the fire.

Lo ringraziate dal cancello e gli dite c.easy: You thank him at the gate and tell him there is no need. Fokke does not insist and is not offended. He nods, turns his wheelbarrow and walks slowly away along the dyke. After a hundred steps he stops, turns and looks at the tower for a long time, the way you look at a house where you lived as a child.
Lo ringraziate dal cancello e gli dite c.short: You thank him and send him away. He goes without a word, but stops on the dyke to gaze at the tower, as one gazes at a childhood home.

Al mercato non si parla d'altro che dell.easy: At the market everyone talks about the two lights. The miller swears they were marsh lights. The schoolmaster says it was a shooting star. The widow Brink says it was the devil, who came to take the master of the estate. He was not ready, she says, so the devil waited four months.
Al mercato non si parla d'altro che dell.short: The market talks only of the two lights: marsh lights, says the miller; a shooting star, says the schoolmaster; the devil, says the widow Brink, who waited four months for the master.

Al Farmer's Market, tra le ceste di arin.easy: At the Farmer's Market, between the baskets of herring and the cheeses, there is Fokke Tammer's stall, and people are queuing in front of it. He sells his new black peat for half a penny a brick. It burns slowly and makes no smoke, and people say one stack is enough for a week. The other peat-cutters look at him unkindly. They stand with their hands in their pockets, next to carts full of normal peat that nobody buys.
Al Farmer's Market, tra le ceste di arin.short: At the market there is a queue for Fokke Tammer's black peat: smokeless, half a penny a brick. The other peat-cutters glare, their ordinary peat unsold.

Fokke serve tutti con pazienza, senza al.easy: Fokke serves everyone with patience. He never raises his voice, and he gives the right change to the last penny. A year ago he could not count past ten. The bandages on his hands are clean. When he sees you, he smiles and waves you to the front: "The master's family does not wait in line."
Fokke serve tutti con pazienza, senza al.short: Fokke, who could not count past ten a year ago, gives exact change. Seeing you, he smiles and waves you forward: "The master's family does not queue."

Compri una pila di mattoni neri, e Fokke.easy: You buy a stack of black bricks, and Fokke sends a boy to carry it to your house. It burns just as he promised: no smoke, no noise, for days. The house is so warm that in winter you sleep with the windows open. And you sleep very well. Nobody in the family remembers their dreams any more.
Compri una pila di mattoni neri, e Fokke.short: The black peat burns for days without smoke, and the house is warm all winter. Everyone sleeps very well. Nobody remembers their dreams any more.

Fokke ti guarda un momento, poi srotola.easy: Fokke looks at you for a moment. Then, without a word, he unwraps the bandages in front of everyone. There is no burn under them. The skin of his palms is smooth, pink and perfect, like a baby's skin. The lines on his hands, the ones the fortune teller at the market reads for a penny, are not there any more. Fokke wraps the bandages again, carefully, and wishes you a good day.
Fokke ti guarda un momento, poi srotola.short: Without a word Fokke unwraps his bandages. No burns: his palms are smooth as a baby's, and the lines of his hands are gone. He wraps them again and wishes you a good day.

I torbai ti offrono un sorso di gin e mo.easy: The peat-cutters give you a sip of gin and lots of opinions. They say the black peat comes from the place where the light was, and none of them goes there. Fokke goes there alone, at night, and comes back with a full cart and dry clothes. "Fokke was the worst of us all," says the oldest one. "Now he is the best. I do not like it."
I torbai ti offrono un sorso di gin e mo.short: The peat-cutters say the black peat comes from where the light was. Fokke goes alone at night and comes back dry. "He was the worst of us. Now he is the best. I do not like it."

Nel Park, sotto il salice vicino allo st.easy: In the Park, under the willow near the pond, there is a big black dog. He is thin, and his fur is covered in dry mud. It is Bruin, Fokke Tammer's dog. Everyone knows him, because for ten years he walked his master home from the inn every night and kept him standing. Since Fokke got "better", Bruin does not go home. He sleeps under the willow and eats what the children throw to him. When Fokke walks along the road, Bruin growls at him, with the fur on his back standing up, until Fokke is gone.
Nel Park, sotto il salice vicino allo st.short: Under the willow in the Park lives Bruin, Fokke Tammer's dog, who for ten years walked his drunken master home. Since Fokke was "cured", Bruin will not go home, and growls whenever Fokke passes.

Bruin ti segue senza bisogno di guinzagl.easy: Bruin follows you without a lead, as if he was waiting for you. At the estate he eats enough for three dogs, sleeps in front of the tower door and never barks at anyone. Only at some people, when they walk past on the road. You soon learn to notice who they are.
Bruin ti segue senza bisogno di guinzagl.short: Bruin follows you home, sleeps by the tower door and never barks. Except at certain people on the road. You learn to notice who.

Porti Bruin a casa di Fokke, con una cor.easy: You take Bruin to Fokke's house with a rope around his neck. The dog pulls back the whole way. Fokke thanks you, offers you a coffee and closes the door. The next day Bruin is not there: Fokke says he ran away. The week after, at the market, Fokke has a new dog. It is black and big, exactly the same as Bruin. It does not growl at anyone.
Porti Bruin a casa di Fokke, con una cor.short: You drag Bruin back to Fokke. Next day the dog has "run away". A week later Fokke has a new one, black, big, identical. It growls at nobody.

In chiesa, dopo il battesimo del figlio.easy: In church, after the christening of the miller's son, Hester Maas takes you to one side. She is a tall, thin woman. She always carries her leather bag, and she looks like someone who has seen half the village born and the other half die. From the bag she takes a silver pocket watch. It is old and worn. The glass is cracked, and the crest of the estate is engraved on the lid.
In chiesa, dopo il battesimo del figlio.short: After the christening, Hester Maas the midwife takes you aside and shows you a silver pocket watch: old, worn, cracked, with the estate's crest on the lid.

\"Me l'ha dato vostro padre, in pagament.easy: "Your father gave it to me to pay for his last visit," she says. "He said it was his. But his watch was in his waistcoat pocket. I saw it myself: new and shiny, with the same crest. He found this one on the floor of the tower. I do not want it, if it belongs to you." The watch has stopped at a quarter past eleven.
\"Me l'ha dato vostro padre, in pagament.short: "Your father paid me with it. He had his own in his waistcoat, the same, but new. This one he found on the tower floor." It has stopped at a quarter past eleven.

Hester rifiuta il denaro, offesa: era un.easy: Hester will not take the money. She is offended: it was a payment, and she is an honest woman. But she lets you look closely at the watch. Inside the lid, under the crest, someone has scratched some letters and a date with a knife. But the metal is so worn that you cannot read them. The works inside are made in a way you have never seen. They are finer and smaller. More modern.
Hester rifiuta il denaro, offesa: era un.short: Hester refuses the money, offended. Inside the lid someone scratched initials and a date, worn unreadable. The works are finer than any you know. More modern.

Hester annuisce, rimette l'orologio nell.easy: Hester nods, puts the watch back in her bag and takes it home. There she locks it in the drawer where she keeps the Register, the birth certificates and the receipts. From that day, when she meets you in the street, she is the first to say hello.
Hester annuisce, rimette l'orologio nell.short: Hester locks the watch in the drawer with her Register. From then on she always greets you first.

Hester ti guarda a lungo. Poi dice che l.easy: Hester looks at you for a long time. Then she says she already does it: the temperatures, the people who get better, the cold hands. She does not know why. She just feels that one day someone will need it. She promises she will not miss a single name.
Hester ti guarda a lungo. Poi dice che l.short: Hester says she already does: temperatures, recoveries, cold hands. Someone will need it one day. She will not miss a name.

Al Builder's Office il capomastro Lamber.easy: At the Builder's Office, Lambert the master builder shows you his drawing of the tower door. It is made of iron, with three locks and very strong hinges, like the door of a castle. He sent two young workers with iron bars and a smith with a file. The door did not move at all. "The lock has melted from the inside," he says. "Someone welded it with a heat you cannot make with coal. And your father was outside when he died. We found him at the bottom of the tower, with the key in his hand."
Al Builder's Office il capomastro Lamber.short: Lambert the master builder could not move the tower door. "The lock is melted from inside, by a heat no coal can make. And your father died outside, at the foot of the tower, with the key in his hand."

I garzoni lavorano due giorni con lo sca.easy: The young workers use their chisels for two days. In the end they make a hole in the wall as big as a fist, next to the stairs. It is dark inside. Lambert puts his ear to the hole and goes pale. He says something inside is humming, softly, like a beehive. Then it stops. The workers do not want to come back.
I garzoni lavorano due giorni con lo sca.short: After two days of chiselling there is a fist-sized hole. Lambert listens and turns white: something inside hums like a beehive. Then it stops. The lads will not come back.

Lambert è sollevato, e non lo nasconde..easy: Lambert is relieved, and he shows it. He only asks you to pay for half a day of work, and he tells you to leave the things of the dead to the dead. As you leave the office, you notice that his hands are bandaged too. He says he burnt them on the stove.
Lambert è sollevato, e non lo nasconde..short: Lambert, relieved, charges only half a day and advises leaving the dead alone. On the way out you notice his hands are bandaged too. The stove, he says.

Il cimitero di {0} è costruito sull'argi.easy: The {0} cemetery is on the dyke, because it is the only dry place in the village. But even there, if you dig one metre down, you find water. New graves fill with water in one night. Siebe the gravedigger is a small man with one leg shorter than the other. He is waiting for you next to your father's grave, which is still covered with fresh earth.
Il cimitero di {0} è costruito sull'argi.short: The cemetery is on the dyke, the only dry ground, and even there graves fill with water overnight. Siebe the gravedigger waits for you by your father's fresh grave.

Fokke Tammer, ti dice, si è offerto di c.easy: He tells you that Fokke Tammer has offered to cover the grave with his black peat, for free. The old people say that bog peat keeps the dead for ever, and the master of the estate deserves to be kept. Siebe waits for your answer, leaning on his spade. He looks like he hopes you will say no.
Fokke Tammer, ti dice, si è offerto di c.short: Fokke Tammer has offered to cover the grave with his black peat, which "keeps the dead for ever". Siebe, leaning on his spade, clearly hopes you will refuse.

Fokke porta la torba lui stesso, il gior.easy: The next day Fokke brings the peat himself. With his bandaged hands he lays it on the grave, brick by brick, like someone tucking in a blanket. When he finishes, he stays on his knees for a moment and looks. Siebe says that nobody in {0} has ever seen such a well-made grave.
Fokke porta la torba lui stesso, il gior.short: Fokke lays the peat on the grave brick by brick, like tucking in a blanket, and kneels a moment to look. Siebe has never seen a finer grave.

Siebe fa portare una lastra di granito d.easy: Siebe has a granite stone brought from the city. It is heavy and smooth, with your father's name and the two dates. Four men are needed to put it in place. When they finish, Siebe shakes your hand. He looks relieved. "That will keep him down," he says. Then his face goes red, as if he has said too much.
Siebe fa portare una lastra di granito d.short: Four men set the heavy granite slab in place. Siebe shakes your hand, relieved: "That will keep him down." Then he blushes.

Alla Traveling Caravan, tra un dentista.easy: At the Traveling Caravan, between a travelling dentist and a man who sells almanacs, there is a blue cart with a sign in gold letters: STAR WATER – FROM BRUNVEEN – CURES ALL ILLS. The seller is a small man in an old, dented top hat. He is not from here. He sells little bottles of dark water for a florin each, and he has already sold fifty in the village. He laughs and says he takes the water "where the star fell".
Alla Traveling Caravan, tra un dentista.short: A stranger in a battered top hat sells STAR WATER – CURES ALL ILLS at a florin a phial. He has sold fifty already. He draws it, he laughs, "where the star fell".

La boccetta è di vetro verde, con il tap.easy: The little bottle is made of green glass, with a cork and a label drawn by hand: a star falling on a field. At home you open it and smell it: smoke, earth, iron. In your laboratory the water stays cloudy for weeks and never clears. And sometimes, when nobody is looking, the water level goes down by a finger.
La boccetta è di vetro verde, con il tap.short: The green phial smells of smoke, earth and iron. In your laboratory the water stays cloudy for weeks, and when nobody is watching, the level drops.

Il sindaco Wessel ascolta la tua denunci.easy: Mayor Wessel listens to your complaint very carefully and promises to deal with it. The next day the blue cart is not there. People in the village say the seller left in the night without paying the innkeeper. At the inn, on his bed, the landlady found only a pile of wet peat in the shape of a man.
Il sindaco Wessel ascolta la tua denunci.short: The mayor promises to deal with it. Next day the cart is gone, the inn unpaid, and on the seller's bed lies a heap of wet peat in the shape of a man.

Lo segui fino all'argine, nel buio, tene.easy: In the dark you follow him to the dyke, staying far behind. The little man walks into the bog up to his knees, at the exact place where the light was. He fills the bottles one by one, singing. Then he stops singing. He stands still in the water for a whole hour, with his arms by his sides, as if someone were talking to him. When he comes out, his top hat is gone, and he walks straight. He does not limp any more.
Lo segui fino all'argine, nel buio, tene.short: You follow him to the bog. He fills his phials where the light was, singing, then stands silent in the water for an hour, as if listening. He comes out without his hat, and without his limp.

Oggi Fokke Tammer ha portato al mercato.easy: Today Fokke Tammer brought to the market the thing he found in the water, the thing that burnt his hands. He had hidden it in his shed. It is a smooth black stone, as big as a loaf of bread, and heavier than it looks. It is always warm, even in the rain. People who touch it say it makes them thirsty.
Oggi Fokke Tammer ha portato al mercato.short: Today Fokke Tammer brought the thing from the water to market: a smooth black stone the size of a loaf, always warm, even in the rain. Touching it makes you thirsty.

Fokke la mette all'asta. Dice che non è.easy: Fokke is selling it at an auction. He says it is not right for him to keep it. It must go "to someone who will know what to do with it". The professor from the city museum came on the morning train with a lot of money. But at the market, everyone was looking at the family of the estate.
Fokke la mette all'asta. Dice che non è.short: Fokke is auctioning it, "for whoever will know what to do with it". The museum professor came with a fat wallet. But everyone was looking at the family of the estate.

Fokke ti consegna la pietra avvolta in u.easy: Fokke gives you the stone, wrapped in a jute sack. He holds it with both hands, like someone giving you a baby. He tells you to keep it dry. Then he speaks quietly, so that only you can hear: "Never leave it near water. It wants to go back."
Fokke ti consegna la pietra avvolta in u.short: Fokke hands you the stone in a sack, like a baby, and whispers: "Never leave it near water. It wants to go back."

A casa la pietra è calda sul tavolo del.easy: At home the stone is warm on the laboratory table. In a few minutes the room smells of the bog. Its smooth surface has no scratches, no lines, no faults. It is not a mineral you know. That night you get up three times to drink.
A casa la pietra è calda sul tavolo del.short: On your laboratory table the warm stone fills the room with the smell of the bog. It is no mineral you know. That night you get up three times to drink.

Quest'anno a {0} non è morto nessuno. Il.easy: This year nobody in {0} has died. Siebe the gravedigger needs money, so now he works as a carpenter too. Pastor Kalf has had more weddings this year than in all the other years together. The couples get married calmly, without fighting, and without inviting any family from outside the village.
Quest'anno a {0} non è morto nessuno. Il.short: Nobody in {0} died this year. The gravedigger now does carpentry, and the pastor has married more couples than ever: calm, quiet weddings, with no relatives from outside.

Alla tenuta, Bruin, il cane di Fokke, ha.easy: At the estate, Bruin, Fokke's dog, now sits in front of the gate every time a wedding procession goes past. He growls softly, but only at one of the two people getting married. Never at both.
Alla tenuta, Bruin, il cane di Fokke, ha.short: When a wedding goes past the estate, Bruin growls softly at one of the couple. Never at both.

Alla tenuta, intanto, la pietra di {0} s.easy: At the estate, meanwhile, {0}'s stone keeps its felt box warm, and in the laboratory the water jugs are empty every morning.
Alla tenuta, intanto, la pietra di {0} s.short: At the estate {0}'s stone warms its box, and every night the water jugs empty.

Al Town Hall il consiglio si riunisce il.easy: At the Town Hall the council meets on the first Thursday of every month, in a room with wooden walls and a picture of the king. Today Hester Maas has asked to speak. A midwife never does that. She has brought her Register, and she reads from it. Nine people in the village have a body temperature two whole degrees lower than normal. All nine are very healthy. All nine have drunk water from the bog.
Al Town Hall il consiglio si riunisce il.short: At the council, Hester Maas reads from her Register: nine villagers are two degrees colder than normal. All nine are perfectly healthy. All nine drank bog water.

Il sindaco Aldert Wessel la ascolta con.easy: Mayor Aldert Wessel listens with his hands crossed on his belly. He is a big man with a red face, gout and a cough that never goes away. When Hester finishes, he thanks her for working so hard. Then he asks if she has an illness to report, or only good health.
Il sindaco Aldert Wessel la ascolta con.short: Mayor Wessel, big, red and gouty, thanks her for her zeal, and asks whether she has an illness to report, or only good health.

Ti alzi e dici che la levatrice ha ragio.easy: You stand up and say that the midwife is right. The council should forbid the bog water until they know what it is. There is a long silence. Then the mayor thanks you too and asks for a vote. Everyone votes no, except you and Hester. As they leave, the councillors who voted no smile at you, one by one.
Ti alzi e dici che la levatrice ha ragio.short: You say the council should ban the bog water. Long silence. Everyone votes against, except you and Hester, and they all smile at you on the way out.

Fuori, sotto il portico, Hester ti mostr.easy: Outside, under the arches, Hester shows you the page. The first name is Fokke Tammer. Then come Lambert the master builder, Smit the washerwoman, two peat-cutters, a boy who works for the smith, the Mulder boy and the miller's wife. The last name was written last week, with a question mark: Wessel, Aldert, mayor.
Fuori, sotto il portico, Hester ti mostr.short: Outside, Hester shows you the names: Fokke Tammer first, then Lambert, Smit the washerwoman, the miller's wife... and last, with a question mark, the mayor.

Dici che, se la buona salute fosse una m.easy: You say that if good health were an illness, {0} would have an epidemic. The whole council laughs, all at the same time, for too long. Hester closes the Register and leaves without saying goodbye. But the mayor invites you to dinner.
Dici che, se la buona salute fosse una m.short: "If good health were a disease, {0} would have an epidemic." The council laughs together, too long. Hester leaves without a word. The mayor invites you to dinner.

Al Laborer's Union, la stanza sopra la s.easy: The Laborer's Union is a room over the stable, where farm workers are hired by the day. Their drinking water comes from a canal that runs straight from the bog. Until last year nobody drank it: it tasted of rust and gave people stomach ache. Now everyone drinks it, because it is good and fresh, and it takes away tiredness. The workers work from morning to night and never complain. The head of the union is worried: for six months nobody has asked for more pay.
Al Laborer's Union, la stanza sopra la s.short: At the Laborer's Union everyone now drinks the bog canal's water, once undrinkable. The labourers work dawn to dusk without complaint. For six months nobody has asked for a rise.

Il pozzo nuovo costa caro e dà un'acqua.easy: The new well is expensive, and its water is hard and tastes of lime. The workers grumble and cough, and they complain about the heat and about their pay. The head of the union thanks you with tears in his eyes.
Il pozzo nuovo costa caro e dà un'acqua.short: The new well's water tastes of lime. The labourers grumble about the heat and the pay again. The union head thanks you with tears in his eyes.

È davvero buona. È fredda come la neve s.easy: It really is good. It is as cold as melted snow, and it leaves a taste of smoke in your mouth that is quite nice. All afternoon you work without getting tired. In the evening you cannot really remember what you were thinking about. Nothing bad, anyway.
È davvero buona. È fredda come la neve s.short: It is good: cold as snowmelt, with a pleasant taste of smoke. You work all afternoon without tiring, and cannot remember what you thought about. Nothing bad.

La chiesa di {0} è di legno, come tutto.easy: The {0} church is made of wood, like everything else. Its steeple is crooked and its benches are old. Pastor Ewout Kalf is a thin, strict man with a very big voice. This Sunday he talks about Lot's wife and about the things you must not look at. Then, in the same voice, he talks about the stone from the bog. He says it came from the sky, and what comes from the sky when nobody called it does not come from God. It must go back to where they found it. While he speaks, he looks at your bench.
La chiesa di {0} è di legno, come tutto.short: Pastor Kalf, thin and stern, preaches that the stone came from the sky uncalled, and so not from God: it must go back where it was found. He looks at your pew as he says it.

Il pastore ti stringe la mano tra le sue.easy: The pastor holds your hand in both of his for a long time, like the hand of someone who has just found God. He tells you that you are not the only person in {0} who thinks this way. But there are few of you, and fewer every month. He asks you to pray for them. He does not say who they are.
Il pastore ti stringe la mano tra le sue.short: The pastor clasps your hand: you are not alone in thinking so, he says, but you are few, and fewer every month. Pray for them. He does not say whom.

Gli rispondi, davanti a tutti, che una p.easy: In front of everyone you tell him that a stone is just a stone, and that you cannot do science with sermons. The pastor's face goes red, then white. Around you, people nod politely. There are many more of them than you thought. They all have their hands in their pockets.
Gli rispondi, davanti a tutti, che una p.short: You tell him a stone is a stone, and science is not made of sermons. Around you, far more people than you expected nod politely, all with their hands in their pockets.

Jaap Mol, il fabbro, è caduto nel canale.easy: At Easter, Jaap Mol the smith fell into the bog canal. He was drunk. He stayed under the water until his workers pulled him out, half an hour later. Everyone thought he was dead. But he stood up by himself, shook off the water and went back to work. Since then he has never missed a blow with his hammer. His horseshoes are so perfect that horses come from the city to {0} to get them. Jaap does not drink or sing any more, and he has said sorry to everyone he owed money to.
Jaap Mol, il fabbro, è caduto nel canale.short: At Easter Jaap Mol the smith fell drunk into the canal and stayed under for half an hour. He got up and went back to work. Now he never misses a stroke, no longer drinks or sings, and has paid all his debts.

Jaap guarda il tuo disegno della serratu.easy: Jaap looks at your drawing of the lock and turns it around. He says you cannot open a welded door with a key. But he can make a key that heats the lock from the outside, until it melts again. He works on it for three days. In the end there is an iron bar as long as an arm, with a wooden handle and a copper tip. He does not ask for money: "For your father," he says. "He was a good man."
Jaap guarda il tuo disegno della serratu.short: A welded door needs no key, says Jaap, but a rod that will melt the lock again. After three days he gives you one, free: "For your father. He was a good man."

Jaap ci pensa, martellando. Ricorda il f.easy: Jaap thinks while he hammers. He says he remembers the cold, then the dark, then a great silence, like in church when the pastor stops talking. And down there was someone who looked like him, sleeping. "I let him sleep," he says. "He was tired. I was not." Then he goes back to his hammering, and he does not miss once.
Jaap ci pensa, martellando. Ricorda il f.short: Jaap remembers the cold, the dark, a great silence, and someone down there who looked like him, asleep. "I let him sleep. He was tired. I was not."

Al cimitero sull'argine il becchino Sieb.easy: At the cemetery on the dyke, Siebe the gravedigger has a problem. He had to move three old graves for the new wall. When he opened the coffins, they were full of dark water. Inside were people who died twenty years ago. They were whole, with skin brown like leather, in their best clothes, with their hands together. They looked asleep. Siebe says he has seen many like that: the peat keeps everything. But in the third grave, under the coffin, in the water, there was another face. It was young and white, with its eyes closed, and nobody ever buried anyone there. Siebe swears it was the miller's wife. This morning the miller's wife was at the market.
Al cimitero sull'argine il becchino Sieb.short: Moving three old graves, Siebe found the dead intact in dark water, as if asleep: the peat keeps everything. But under the third coffin lay a young face nobody buried there. The miller's wife. Who was at the market this morning.

Li riseppellite al tramonto, in fretta,.easy: You bury them again at sunset, quickly, with dry earth from the hill, so that the water cannot reach them. Before he fills the third grave, Siebe looks away and says a prayer that is not in the pastor's book. When you finish, he washes his hands three times at the fountain and asks you not to tell anyone.
Li riseppellite al tramonto, in fretta,.short: You rebury them at sunset in dry earth. At the third grave Siebe looks away and says a prayer not in the pastor's book, then asks you to tell nobody.

Hester arriva con la borsa e la lanterna.easy: Hester comes with her bag and her lantern. In the third grave the water is cloudy now, and you cannot see the face. Hester puts her thermometer in the water, waits, and takes it out. The water down there is as warm as a sleeping body. She writes it in the Register. Then she closes the book and says she has seen nothing, and that it is better this way.
Hester arriva con la borsa e la lanterna.short: In the third grave the water has clouded over the face. Hester's thermometer says it is as warm as a sleeping body. She writes it down, then says she saw nothing.

Quattro anni dalla notte delle due luci..easy: It is four years since the night of the two lights. Since then nobody in {0} has died of an illness. Only two old people died in their sleep, and a child fell from the hayloft. Every summer the marsh fever used to kill someone, but this year it did not come. The doctor from the city says it is thanks to the air. I count the temperatures.
Quattro anni dalla notte delle due luci..short: Four years since the two lights, and nobody in {0} has died of illness. Even the marsh fever stayed away. The city doctor says it is the air. I count the temperatures.

Il cane di Fokke Tammer vive alla tenuta.easy: Fokke Tammer's dog lives at the estate. He growls at the same people that I write in the Register. Now I take him with me when I visit the houses. He is never wrong.
Il cane di Fokke Tammer vive alla tenuta.short: Fokke's dog growls at the very people I mark in the Register. I take him on my rounds now. He is never wrong.

Il cane nuovo di Fokke Tammer, quello id.easy: Fokke Tammer's new dog, the one that looks exactly like the old one, follows its master everywhere without a sound. It does not bark, it does not eat, and it does not get older. The children do not play with it any more.
Il cane nuovo di Fokke Tammer, quello id.short: Fokke's new dog follows him everywhere in silence. It does not bark, eat or age. The children no longer play with it.

L'acqua della stella, quella del vendito.easy: The star water, from the seller in the top hat, is now in every kitchen. People tell me that one of the little bottles is on the laboratory table at the estate.
L'acqua della stella, quella del vendito.short: The star water is in every kitchen now. One phial, I am told, is in the estate's laboratory.

Il venditore dell'acqua della stella è s.easy: The seller of the star water has gone, but the water has not. Now the innkeeper's son sells it, with the same label.
Il venditore dell'acqua della stella è s.short: The seller is gone, but the innkeeper's son sells his star water, same label.

Il venditore dell'acqua della stella è t.easy: The seller of the star water came back this year. He has no top hat, no limp, and not the same accent as before. He talks like us.
Il venditore dell'acqua della stella è t.short: The star water seller is back, without hat, limp or accent. He talks like us.

Sulla tomba del signore della tenuta la.easy: On the grave of the master of the estate, no grass or moss has grown on Fokke's peat. It is still black and smooth, like on the first day.
Sulla tomba del signore della tenuta la.short: On the master's grave Fokke's peat grows nothing. It is as black as the first day.

La lastra di granito sulla tomba del sig.easy: The granite stone on the master's grave has moved a little to one side, as if something under it were pushing. Siebe says it is only the ground settling.
La lastra di granito sulla tomba del sig.short: The granite slab on the master's grave has tilted, as if pushed from below. Siebe says it is the ground settling.

La famiglia della tenuta è benvoluta, or.easy: Now people like the family of the estate. They invite them to parties and say hello to them by name. I am afraid for them.
La famiglia della tenuta è benvoluta, or.short: The estate family is well liked now. I am afraid for them.

La famiglia della tenuta fa domande, e i.easy: The family of the estate asks questions, and the village does not answer any more. People still say hello to them, always politely. But nobody goes to visit them now.
La famiglia della tenuta fa domande, e i.short: The estate family asks questions; the village no longer answers. Polite greetings, and no visits.

Il sindaco Wessel non tossisce più e ha.easy: Mayor Wessel does not cough any more, and he does not limp. In one winter he lost forty pounds, with no diet and no medicine, and his gout disappeared in one night. Now the council meetings last ten minutes. Nobody says no to anything any more.
Il sindaco Wessel non tossisce più e ha.short: Mayor Wessel no longer coughs or limps: he lost forty pounds in a winter, and his gout vanished overnight. Council sittings now last ten minutes. Nobody objects to anything.

Il mulino, senza Harm Visser, macina meg.easy: Without Harm Visser, the mill works better than before. Grietje runs it alone, and she never gets the weight of a sack wrong.
Il mulino, senza Harm Visser, macina meg.short: Without Harm Visser the mill grinds better. Grietje runs it alone, and never misweighs a sack.

Al mulino Harm Visser e sua moglie Griet.easy: At the mill Harm Visser and his wife Grietje sing together while they work, with two voices. They are perfectly in tune.
Al mulino Harm Visser e sua moglie Griet.short: At the mill Harm and Grietje Visser sing in two parts as they work. Perfectly in tune.

Alla Bank, la casa più solida del paese,.easy: At the Bank, the strongest house in the village, with the only safe in the province, Professor Ostrander is waiting for you. He works at the natural history museum in the city. He is an old gentleman with gold glasses and a stiff white collar. He says he could not buy the stone at the auction, and he does not blame anyone. But science has its rights. He only needs a tiny piece, as small as a fingernail, to study it. He already has the money ready in an envelope.
Alla Bank, la casa più solida del paese,.short: At the Bank, Professor Ostrander of the city museum asks politely for a chip of the stone, no bigger than a fingernail, for science. The money is ready in an envelope.

La pietra non si lascia scalfire da nien.easy: Nothing can scratch the stone: not a knife, not a file, not a hammer. In the end Jaap Mol the smith does it, with one exact blow. The professor puts the chip in a little velvet box and leaves on the evening train. A few months later you read in the city newspaper that the museum's caretaker, who was ill for years, is now well. And the professor does not drink any more.
La pietra non si lascia scalfire da nien.short: Only Jaap Mol's single precise blow can chip the stone. The professor leaves with it in a velvet box. Months later the city paper says the museum caretaker is cured, and the professor has stopped drinking.

Il professore ripone la busta, deluso ma.easy: The professor puts the envelope away. He is disappointed but polite. He gives you his card, "in case you change your mind". On the way back to the station he stops on the dyke and looks at the bog. He stays there a long time. Then he gets on the train.
Il professore ripone la busta, deluso ma.short: The professor leaves his card, "in case you change your mind". On the way to the station he stops a long time on the dyke, looking at the bog.

La Church Library è una stanza dietro la.easy: The Church Library is a room behind the sacristy, with three hundred books and a stove that smokes. Pastor Kalf has left you the keys and a book open on the reading stand. It is a German book from a hundred years ago about the bog people. It says that bodies have been found in the peat after a thousand years, with their skin and hair still whole, as if they were sleeping. Some had a rope around the neck, others had their hands tied. The book says they were all buried alive. Nobody knows why.
La Church Library è una stanza dietro la.short: The pastor has left a German treatise open for you: bodies found in the peat after a thousand years, intact, as if asleep. All buried alive, it says. Nobody knows why.

A margine, nella grafia del pastore: *E.easy: In the margin, in the pastor's handwriting: *What if nobody buried them? What if they went in by themselves?*
A margine, nella grafia del pastore: *E.short: In the margin, in the pastor's hand: *What if they went in by themselves?*

Studi per tre sere, al lume della candel.easy: You study for three evenings by candlelight. You learn how peat keeps a body, how the dark water turns it into leather, and how to tell a body hundreds of years old from one that died yesterday. You also learn to know the smell. On your way home, you smell it everywhere.
Studi per tre sere, al lume della candel.short: Three evenings by candlelight teach you how peat preserves the dead, and the smell of it. On the way home you smell it everywhere.

Il pastore accetta subito, come se aspet.easy: The pastor says yes immediately, as if he was only waiting for someone to ask. The first night watch of {0} goes out the next Saturday: the pastor, three peat-cutters, Siebe the gravedigger and a lantern. They find nothing. But all night, from the houses, people watch them walk past, behind the windows, in the dark.
Il pastore accetta subito, come se aspet.short: The pastor agrees at once. The first night watch, five men and a lantern, finds nothing. But all night people watch them from dark windows.

Il sindaco Aldert Wessel ti riceve nel s.easy: Mayor Aldert Wessel meets you in his office at the Town Hall. He is thin, he stands straight, his face is pink, and his collar is too big for him. He offers you a glass of water and asks, very politely, what you need. He remembers your mother's name, your birthday, and the exact price the estate paid for hay last year. When you shake his hand, it is cold. Old Wessel always had sweaty hands. In the village they called him "the fish".
Il sindaco Aldert Wessel ti riceve nel s.short: Mayor Wessel, thin and rosy now, remembers your mother's name, your birthday, the price of your hay. His hand is cold. Old Wessel's hands were always sweaty: they called him "the fish".

Lo dici ad alta voce, ridendo, come una.easy: You say it out loud, laughing, like a joke: "Mayor, have you caught a cold?" Nobody laughs. The mayor looks at you with pale, patient eyes. He says the doctor from the city told him to take cold baths, and he feels like a new man. The councillors nod, one after the other. As you leave, you count seven of them with their hands in their pockets.
Lo dici ad alta voce, ridendo, come una.short: "Mayor, have you caught a chill?" Nobody laughs. Cold baths, he says patiently: he feels reborn. On your way out you count seven councillors with their hands in their pockets.

Sorridi, ringrazi, bevi il bicchiere d'a.easy: You smile, you say thank you, and you drink half the glass of water. At home, in your notebook, you write the mayor's name under Fokke Tammer's. The list is already long. You notice that you are writing the names in order of how kind they are.
Sorridi, ringrazi, bevi il bicchiere d'a.short: At home you add the mayor to the list under Fokke Tammer. It is already long. You realise you are writing the names in order of kindness.

Il sindaco sorride: la signora Wessel st.easy: The mayor smiles: Mrs Wessel is very well, thank you. In the spring she went to the city, to her sister's house, to rest. She writes to him every week. He shows you the letters: a tidy pile, tied with a ribbon. All the envelopes are the same. All the handwriting is the same. And the postmark is always the same: {0}.
Il sindaco sorride: la signora Wessel st.short: Mrs Wessel is resting at her sister's in the city, he smiles, and writes every week. He shows you the letters: identical envelopes, identical hand, and every postmark says {0}.

Alla Foundry, sul canale, il padrone Dir.easy: At the Foundry, on the canal, the owner Dirk Haverkamp shows you a bill that was never paid. It is from 1864, and your father signed it. Haverkamp's father left it to him together with the foundry. The bill is for a brass ring three metres wide, in twelve parts; thirty-six pieces of black glass from Bohemia; and two hundred metres of copper wire. It is a lot of money. Haverkamp still has the original drawings, with your father's measurements and notes, and a twelfth spare part that your father never came to take.
Alla Foundry, sul canale, il padrone Dir.short: At the Foundry, Dirk Haverkamp shows you your father's unpaid bill of 1864: a brass ring in twelve sections, black glass, copper wire. He still has the drawings, and a spare segment never collected.

Haverkamp ti consegna un rotolo di diseg.easy: Haverkamp gives you a roll of drawings tied with string, and the spare part wrapped in oilcloth. On the drawings, next to the measurements, your father wrote some words in pencil that you do not understand: *resonance*, *return*, *receiver*. At the bottom of the page there is a question, with three circles around it: *who transmits?*
Haverkamp ti consegna un rotolo di diseg.short: Haverkamp gives you the drawings and the spare segment. Beside the measurements your father wrote *resonance*, *return*, *receiver*, and, circled three times: *who transmits?*

Haverkamp non insiste. Dice che terrà i.easy: Haverkamp does not insist. He says he will keep the drawings in a drawer until someone from the family comes to pay. "Sooner or later you will come," he says, very sure. "Your father always said it: the numbers add up in the end. Even the ones that do not."
Haverkamp non insiste. Dice che terrà i.short: Haverkamp will keep the drawings until the family pays. "You will come. Your old man always said: the sums add up. Even the ones that do not."

Al Farmer's Apprentice, il podere dove i.easy: At the Farmer's Apprentice, the farm where the village children learn to milk cows and cut hay, the widow Brink is waiting for you. She is holding her apron tight in her hands. Her son Piet is fifteen. In September he fell into the bog while he was running after a calf. He came home the next morning, alone and dry. Since then he is the best boy on the farm. He obeys, he works, and he learns everything the first time. He has never been rude to her again. He has never cried again. Last night she asked him if he loved her. He said yes, at once, with a beautiful smile.
Al Farmer's Apprentice, il podere dove i.short: The widow Brink's son Piet, fifteen, fell into the bog in September and came home next morning, dry. Now he is the best boy on the farm: obedient, tireless, never rude, never in tears. "Do you love me?" "Yes," at once, with a lovely smile.

La vedova ti guarda come si guarda qualc.easy: The widow looks at you like someone who knows you lied to be kind, and she thanks you anyway. Behind her, Piet smiles. From that day the widow does not come to the farm any more. Piet does. He is always the first to arrive and the last to leave.
La vedova ti guarda come si guarda qualc.short: The widow thanks you as one thanks a kind liar. Behind her, Piet smiles. She never comes back to the farm. Piet is always first to arrive, last to leave.

Hester visita Piet nella cucina dei Brin.easy: Hester examines Piet in the Brinks' kitchen with the door closed. After an hour she comes out. She writes a temperature and a sentence in the Register, and she does not let you read it. Then she sits next to the widow and holds her hands. They stay like that, without talking, while outside Piet chops wood, again and again, always at the same speed.
Hester visita Piet nella cucina dei Brin.short: After an hour with Piet behind a closed door, Hester writes something she will not show you. Then she holds the widow's hands in silence, while outside Piet chops wood at an unchanging rhythm.

Al punto dove è caduto Piet, l'acqua è f.easy: At the place where Piet fell, the water is still and black. There are bubbles on top of it that do not burst. The widow kneels on the bank and softly calls her son's name, the way she did when he was little. For a moment you think you see a white face under the water, with its eyes closed, turning towards her voice. Then nothing.
Al punto dove è caduto Piet, l'acqua è f.short: Where Piet fell, the water is black and still. The widow kneels and softly calls his name. For a moment a white face under the water seems to turn towards her voice. Then nothing.

Il pastore Kalf è venuto alla tenuta, ve.easy: Pastor Kalf came to the estate. He is old now, with his walking stick and his hat in his hand. He asked to speak to the whole family. He said that he has also been counting, all these years: the weddings, the christenings, the confessions. Nobody in {0} confesses any more. They have no sins.
Il pastore Kalf è venuto alla tenuta, ve.short: Old Pastor Kalf came to the estate to speak to the whole family. He too has been counting. Nobody in {0} confesses any more. They have no sins.

Ha chiesto alla famiglia di riportare la.easy: He asked the family to take the stone back to the bog, to the exact place where the light was, and to leave it there. "We do not know what it does," he said, "but we know it works better near water. So at least let it work far from your houses." Then he waited for the answer standing up, because the chair they offered him was next to the fire.
Ha chiesto alla famiglia di riportare la.short: He asked you to return the stone to the place of the light: "We do not know what it does, but it does it better near water. Let it do it far from your houses." He waited standing, because the chair was by the fire.

Prima di andarsene ha benedetto la casa,.easy: Before he left, he blessed the house, room by room, even the closed tower. He said that the family, whatever it decides, has always been on the right side.
Prima di andarsene ha benedetto la casa,.short: Before leaving he blessed every room, even the tower: whatever you decide, he said, you have always been on the right side.

Prima di andarsene ha guardato a lungo c.easy: Before he left, he looked for a long time at the person who argued with him years ago, on the church steps. He said nothing. He looked more sad than angry.
Prima di andarsene ha guardato a lungo c.short: Before leaving he looked long at whoever had argued with him on the church steps, years ago. More sad than angry.

All'alba portate la pietra all'argine, a.easy: At dawn you carry the stone to the dyke in its sack and give it to Pastor Kalf. He walks into the bog up to his waist, with his long black robe floating on the water, to the place where the light was. He lets the stone go. It sinks with no sound and no bubbles, as if the water was waiting for it. For a moment the water all around becomes as smooth as glass. Then the wind moves it again.
All'alba portate la pietra all'argine, a.short: At dawn Pastor Kalf wades waist-deep to the place of the light and lets the stone go. It sinks without a bubble, as if expected. For a moment the water turns to glass. Then the wind breaks it.

Ringraziate il pastore e gli dite di no:.easy: You thank the pastor and say no. The stone is something to study, and the family of the estate is a family of scientists. The pastor nods, puts his hat on and walks slowly away along the dyke. That evening the stone stays on the shelf in the laboratory, warm, in its box lined with felt. At night, everyone in the house gets up to drink. Nobody tells the others.
Ringraziate il pastore e gli dite di no:.short: You refuse: the stone is for study. The pastor leaves without a word. That night the stone stays warm on the laboratory shelf, and everyone in the house gets up to drink. Nobody tells the others.

Il ferro di Jaap Mol, il fabbro, scalda.easy: The iron rod of Jaap Mol the smith heats the lock for an hour, until the metal is red and melts like wax. The tower door opens, with a cry from its hinges, twenty-three years later.
Il ferro di Jaap Mol, il fabbro, scalda.short: Jaap Mol's iron melts the lock like wax. The tower door groans open, twenty-three years later.

Lambert, il capomastro, allarga il vecch.easy: Lambert the master builder makes the old hole in the wall bigger, until a person can get through. He does not want to go in first. Nobody wants to.
Lambert, il capomastro, allarga il vecch.short: Lambert widens the old hole until a person fits. Nobody wants to go in first.

Ci vogliono quattro uomini, due leve e u.easy: Four men with two iron bars need a whole day to make a hole in the tower wall, next to the welded door. As soon as they finish, the workers leave, without waiting for their money.
Ci vogliono quattro uomini, due leve e u.short: Four men take a whole day to break through beside the welded door, and leave without waiting for their pay.

La scala sale a spirale nel buio, fino a.easy: The stairs go round and round up into the dark, to the room with the four big windows. There is dust, there are cobwebs, and there is a smell of burnt copper. In the middle of the room, on a wooden frame, there is a brass ring twice as tall as a man. It is made of twelve parts, and the inside edge is covered with pieces of black glass. It is not working. One of the glass pieces is broken, and in the crack there is a small piece of smooth black stone, exactly like the stone from the bog.
La scala sale a spirale nel buio, fino a.short: At the top of the spiral stair, among dust and the smell of burnt copper, stands a brass ring twice a man's height, lined with black glass. One pane is cracked, and in the crack is a chip of black stone, like the stone from the bog.

Il pavimento, sotto l'anello, è bruciato.easy: Under the ring, the floor is burnt in a perfect circle. On the table, next to the window that looks at the bog, is your father's notebook. It is open at a page with a ribbon in it. There are calculations, distances and angles. Then, at the bottom, there is a line that is not crazy at all:
Il pavimento, sotto l'anello, è bruciato.short: Under the ring the floor is burnt in a perfect circle. By the window, your father's notebook lies open at a marked page. At the bottom, a line that is no raving:

*11 novembre, ore undici e quattordici m.easy: *11 November, fourteen minutes past eleven. Light on the ring. At the same moment, light on the bog, twelve hundred metres away, to the north-north-east. The Machine is a bridge: one end is here, the other is there. Something came over the bridge from the other side. And I did not open any bridge.*
*11 novembre, ore undici e quattordici m.short: *11 November, 11:14. Light on the ring, and at the same instant on the bog, twelve hundred metres away. The Machine is a bridge. Something crossed it from the other side, and I opened no bridge.*

**Le due luci erano una cosa sola. La pi.easy: **The two lights were one thing. The stone did not fall from the sky. Your father's Machine, a machine that moves things from one place to another, put it in the bog on the night it turned on by itself.** The old man was not crazy: something came through. Now you must find out where it came from.
**Le due luci erano una cosa sola. La pi.short: **The two lights were one. Your father's Machine, which moves things from place to place, put the stone in the bog the night it turned on by itself.** Something did come through. But from where?

Sul tavolo, accanto al quaderno, srotola.easy: On the table, next to the notebook, you open the drawings you bought at the foundry. They match the ring, part by part. Only one part is missing: the broken one. Luckily, you have the spare part.
Sul tavolo, accanto al quaderno, srotola.short: The foundry drawings match the ring exactly. Only the cracked segment is missing, and luckily you have the spare.

Lo leggete a turno, fino all'alba, alla.easy: You take turns reading it until morning, by candlelight, in the room with the ring.
