But since that day the lanterns of the Watch have stayed at home. At night, from the bell tower, I see the road on the dyke full of people in nightshirts, walking towards the bog.
La famiglia della tenuta ha accettato la.short: The estate family took the council's medal. I do not blame them. But the Watch no longer goes out, and at night I see the dyke road full of people in nightshirts, walking to the bog.

La famiglia della tenuta ha rifiutato la.easy: The family of the estate said no to the council's medal. Our father is proud of them. In the village people are so perfectly kind to them that it hurts to watch. At the market they serve them last, with a smile.
La famiglia della tenuta ha rifiutato la.short: The estate family refused the medal. Father is proud. The village is so perfectly kind to them it hurts to watch.

La Ronda di {0} esce ancora, due notti a.easy: {0}'s Watch still goes out two nights a week. I bring hot tea. There are not many of us now, but we all sing out of tune beautifully.
La Ronda di {0} esce ancora, due notti a.short: {0}'s Watch still goes out twice a week. I bring tea. We are few, but we all sing beautifully out of tune.

Gerrit Tammer, il figlio del torbaio, sc.easy: Gerrit Tammer, the peat-cutter's son, is still digging at the Park, at the place where the light was. He says he is close. Close to what, he does not say. Please, Willem, do not come back to {0}. Stay where it is hot, where people sweat and complain and die of fever. Here nobody dies any more, and I am afraid that I will not be able to die either. Your Trijntje.
Gerrit Tammer, il figlio del torbaio, sc.short: Gerrit Tammer still digs at the place of the light. He says he is close. Willem, do not come back. Stay where people sweat and complain and die of fever. Here nobody dies, and I fear I will not manage to either. Trijntje.

Sogni l'argine, di notte, e i tuoi piedi.easy: You dream of the dyke at night, and of your bare feet on the wet grass. You walk towards the bog, but you do not want to, and you are not cold. At the place where the light was, someone is standing in the water up to the chest, waiting for you. They have your face, your hair, your clothes. They reach out a hand to you, with a smile so peaceful that you want to cry. Further away, under the water, your parents are sleeping.
Sogni l'argine, di notte, e i tuoi piedi.short: You dream of walking barefoot to the bog. Waiting chest-deep at the place of the light is someone with your face, smiling so serenely you want to weep. Beyond, under the water, your parents sleep.

Sogni la tenuta com'era nella tua infanz.easy: You dream of the estate as it was when you were a child, with your parents at the kitchen table. The person who brought you up pours you a glass of dark water from the jug. They tell you to drink it, because it is good for you. They drank it only once, and it was the calmest evening of their life. The hands on the jug are white. Outside the window, the bog is smoking.
Sogni la tenuta com'era nella tua infanz.short: You dream of your childhood kitchen. The one who raised you pours you dark water: drink, it is good for you. Their hands on the jug are white. Outside, the bog smokes.

Sogni la torre, con la porta saldata e l.easy: You dream of the tower, with its welded door and its dark windows. You climb the spiral stairs and never get to the top. The steps go on and on, and above you something hums softly, like bees in a wall. Halfway up you find a silver watch on a step. Its glass is cracked. It says a quarter past eleven. You pick it up, and it is warm.
Sogni la torre, con la porta saldata e l.short: You dream of climbing the tower's endless stair towards a humming like bees. On a step lies a silver watch, cracked, at a quarter past eleven. It is warm.

Vai avanti, e il sogno diventa dolce, le.easy: You go on, and the dream becomes sweet and very slow, with no fear. You wake up at dawn with cold hands and a peace that is not yours. It takes an hour to go away.
Vai avanti, e il sogno diventa dolce, le.short: You go on, and the dream turns sweet. You wake with cold hands and a peace not your own. It takes an hour to fade.

Vai avanti, e la scala finisce di colpo:.easy: You go on, and suddenly the stairs end. In front of you is the brass ring, lit up, white. You wake up at dawn with the watch in your hand. No: your hand is closed tight around nothing, as if you were really holding it.
Vai avanti, e la scala finisce di colpo:.short: The stair ends at the brass ring, lit white. You wake at dawn clutching the watch. No: clutching nothing, as if it were there.

Ti svegli di colpo, nel tuo letto, con i.easy: You wake up suddenly in your bed, with your heart beating hard. You touch your hands: they are warm. You cannot sleep again until dawn. You listen to the silence of {0}. It is deeper than you remember.
Ti svegli di colpo, nel tuo letto, con i.short: You wake with a start. Your hands are warm. Until dawn you lie listening to {0}'s silence, deeper than you remembered.

La mattina dopo, a colazione, nessuno ra.easy: The next morning, at breakfast, nobody talks about their dream. You all look at your hands secretly, over your cups. From the window you can see the bog, flat and grey, and the tower, straight against the sky. Someone at the gate is already ringing the bell. It is a man from the council.
La mattina dopo, a colazione, nessuno ra.short: At breakfast nobody tells their dream. You all check your hands, over your cups. At the gate, a gentleman from the council is already ringing.

Al Park, d'inverno, lo stagno gela, e i.easy: In winter the pond in the Park freezes, and the children of {0} skate on it, all together, in a circle. They never bump into each other. All except one: the youngest child in Miss Borg's class. He is eight, and he skates badly. He falls, laughs, cries and gets up again. Today he fell where the ice is thin, near the canal to the bog, and the ice broke. The other children stopped on the bank, in a line, and they are watching. Nobody shouts. The boy holds on to the edge, and the dark water is up to his chin.
Al Park, d'inverno, lo stagno gela, e i.short: The children skate in a perfect circle, except the youngest in Miss Borg's class, who falls, laughs and cries. Today the thin ice by the canal broke under him. The others watch from the bank in a row. Nobody shouts. The dark water is at his chin.

L'acqua è così fredda che per un istante.easy: The water is so cold that for a moment you feel nothing: not your hands, not your heart, not your fear. It is a wonderful feeling. Then the child holds on to your neck, crying, and the cold comes back, terrible and human. You carry him to the bank. Miss Borg runs up and wraps you both in her shawl. The child shakes and screams for an hour. It is the most beautiful sound you have ever heard.
L'acqua è così fredda che per un istante.short: The cold is so deep that for an instant you feel nothing, and it is wonderful. Then the child clings to you, sobbing, and the cold returns, terrible and human. He screams for an hour. The most beautiful sound you have ever heard.

Ti sdrai sul ghiaccio, allunghi un ramo,.easy: You lie on the ice and reach out with a branch. The child grabs it the second time. You pull him out, wet through, blue with cold, his teeth chattering. He is all right. While you carry him back to the bank, the children standing in a line look at you with empty faces. Then they go back to skating, in a circle, all together, as if nothing has happened.
Ti sdrai sul ghiaccio, allunghi un ramo,.short: Flat on the ice, you reach him with a branch and pull him out, blue and chattering, but well. The children on the bank watch blankly, then go back to their perfect circle.

Al Laborer's Union, il vecchio capo del.easy: At the Laborer's Union, Teun Bos, the old head of the workers' union, is closing the office for ever. Nobody needs a union now, he says. Nobody asks for more pay, nobody complains about working hours, nobody gets hurt. The help fund for widows and sick people is full: in twenty years nobody has needed it. Teun would like to give it to the estate, "because you still get ill". Or he could give it to the council, which wants it to build a new fountain in the square.
Al Laborer's Union, il vecchio capo del.short: Teun Bos is closing the union for good: nobody complains, nobody gets hurt. The fund for widows and the sick is untouched after twenty years. He would give it to the estate, "who still fall ill", or to the council, for a new fountain.

Teun ti consegna la cassa di latta con l.easy: Teun gives you the tin box with the coins and the book of payments, and shakes your hand. His hand is warm and rough. "Use it for the people who are still ill," he says. When the council hears about it, they send you a letter of congratulations. It is very kind.
Teun ti consegna la cassa di latta con l.short: Teun gives you the tin box: "Use it for those still unwell." The council sends a most kind letter of congratulations.

La fontana nuova viene inaugurata in pri.easy: The new fountain opens in the spring. It is made of bronze and marble, with three mouths that pour dark water straight from the bog canal. The children drink from it when they come out of school. On the opening day Teun Bos drinks from it too, and stops coughing.
La fontana nuova viene inaugurata in pri.short: The new bronze fountain pours dark water straight from the bog. The children drink there after school. On the opening day Teun Bos drinks too, and stops coughing.

Teun annuisce, lentamente, e rimette la.easy: Teun nods slowly and puts the box back under the floor, where he always kept it. He gives you the key to the office, "just in case", and leaves. In the book of payments the last page is empty, with a date at the top. Teun has left it like that for the next person.
Teun annuisce, lentamente, e rimette la.short: Teun hides the box under the floor again and gives you the key, "just in case". The last page of the register is blank but for a date, left for whoever comes after.

Sono tornata in paese a giugno, dopo qua.easy: I came back to the village in June, after four years in the field hospitals of Flanders. I brought a suitcase, a medal I did not ask for, and grandmother Hester's broken watch in my pocket. My father Joost died last winter of influenza, with a fever of thirty-nine degrees. The telegram told me so, and I was glad. He left me his surgery and this Register.
Sono tornata in paese a giugno, dopo qua.short: Back in the village after four years in the field hospitals of Flanders, with grandmother Hester's broken watch. My father died last winter with a fever of thirty-nine: I was glad. He left me this Register.

Il paese è diventato una cittadina: la l.easy: The village is a small town now. It has electric light, a telephone at the Town Hall, a University with three departments, two newspapers and a cooperative bank. The streets are clean. The people are kind, healthy and hard-working. It is the quietest place I have ever been to, and I have just come back from the war.
Il paese è diventato una cittadina: la l.short: The village is a town now: electric light, a University, two newspapers. Clean streets, kind and healthy people. The quietest place I have ever known, and I have come from the war.

I ragazzi partiti volontari sono tornati.easy: Almost all the young men who went as volunteers have come back. That is what worries me. At the front millions died. Forty left the village, and thirty-eight came back, healthy, with no scars and no bad dreams. The band was waiting for them at the station, and at the fountain in the square there was a glass of dark water for each of them, "to say welcome home".
I ragazzi partiti volontari sono tornati.short: Forty left for the war and thirty-eight came back, without a scar or a nightmare. Millions died out there. At the station, the band; at the fountain, a glass of dark water each, "for welcome home".

Gli eredi della tenuta sono tornati anch.easy: The heirs of the estate have come back too. Tomorrow I will visit them, one by one, and sign a certificate of good health for each of them. The council asks for one for everyone back from the war. I will only sign it after I have taken their temperature.
Gli eredi della tenuta sono tornati anch.short: The heirs of the estate are back too. Tomorrow I will sign their certificates of good health, as the council requires. But only after I have measured.

Bandiere a ogni finestra, la banda in pi.easy: There are flags at every window, the band is in the square, and the soldiers who came back stand in the front row in front of the Town Hall, with medals on their chests. The dark water is everywhere: in the fountains, in the jugs at the cafés, in the glasses for the toast. In {0} they now just call it "the water".
Bandiere a ogni finestra, la banda in pi.short: Flags, a band, the returned soldiers in the front row with their medals. Dark water everywhere: fountains, carafes, toasting glasses. In {0} they just call it "the water" now.

La famiglia della tenuta siede in prima.easy: The family of the estate sits in the front row, in the place of honour that the council gave it years ago, with the silver medals on their chests. Behind you, three hundred people are looking at the backs of your heads.
La famiglia della tenuta siede in prima.short: The estate family sits in the place of honour, silver medals on. Behind you, three hundred people watch the backs of your heads.

Per la famiglia della tenuta non è previ.easy: There is no seat for the family of the estate. You stand at the back of the square, next to Trijntje Kalf and Miss Borg. Nobody asks you to go away.
Per la famiglia della tenuta non è previ.short: No seats for the estate family. You stand at the back with Trijntje Kalf and Miss Borg. Nobody asks you to leave.

Al Town Hall, nel salone delle cerimonie.easy: At the Town Hall, in the big hall, there is a party for the soldiers who came back. Mayor Bram Wessel, old Aldert's son, gives a short, perfect speech about sacrifice and peace. Then the waiters walk among the guests with trays of crystal glasses full of dark water, "the best in the province". The mayor raises his glass. Three hundred people raise theirs at the same moment. Everyone is looking at you.
Al Town Hall, nel salone delle cerimonie.short: After Mayor Bram Wessel's perfect speech, waiters bring crystal glasses of dark water. The mayor raises his; three hundred people raise theirs at the same moment. Everyone is looking at you.

Bevi. Il salone applaude, e tu senti l'a.easy: You drink. The hall claps, and the applause feels like a hug. For the rest of the evening everything is easy: the words, the smiles, the cold handshakes. You walk home, softly singing the Sunday hymn, and you do not know that you know it by heart.
Bevi. Il salone applaude, e tu senti l'a.short: You drink, and the applause feels like an embrace. All evening everything is easy. You walk home humming the Sunday hymn, not knowing you know it by heart.

Con un gesto piccolo, mentre tutti bevon.easy: While everyone drinks, you quietly pour the water into the vase of lilies. Nobody notices, or it seems that way. The next day the lilies in that vase are perfect: open, white and sweet-smelling. The lilies in the other vases are dead.
Con un gesto piccolo, mentre tutti bevon.short: While everyone drinks, you tip the water into the lilies. Nobody seems to notice. Next day those lilies are perfect. All the others have wilted.

Tiri fuori dalla giacca una fiaschetta d.easy: You take a little bottle of wine out of your jacket and make the toast with that, smiling. The silence lasts a moment too long. Then the mayor laughs politely, and everyone laughs with him. For the rest of the evening, at the table, nobody pours you anything.
Tiri fuori dalla giacca una fiaschetta d.short: You toast with wine from your own flask. The silence lasts a moment too long; then the mayor laughs, and everyone with him. Nobody pours you anything else all evening.

Alla Credit Union, la banca cooperativa.easy: At the Credit Union, the cooperative bank that the council started after the war, Mayor Bram Wessel meets you in the manager's office. He is fifty-four. His grey hair is carefully combed, and he has his father's amazing memory. Old Aldert died ten years ago, he says, of old age, in his sleep. He was a happy man. The council has made many decisions since the war, and one of them is about your family.
Alla Credit Union, la banca cooperativa.short: At the Credit Union, Mayor Bram Wessel, fifty-four, grey and precise as his father, says old Aldert died happy in his sleep. The council has made a decision about your family.

Vorrebbe comprare la pietra di {0}. Non.easy: He wants to buy {0}'s stone. Not for himself, but for the village. He would put it in the bog, where it belongs, "where it is good for everyone". He offers so much money that your head spins. The contract is already written.
Vorrebbe comprare la pietra di {0}. Non.short: He wants to buy {0}'s stone for the village, to put it in the bog "where it does everyone good". The sum is dizzying. The contract is ready.

Vorrebbe che la pietra restasse dov'è, n.easy: He wants the stone to stay where it is, in the bog, for ever. The council has voted to protect the place where the light was, like a town monument, with a fence and a guard. He asks the family not to take it out, "for the good of everyone".
Vorrebbe che la pietra restasse dov'è, n.short: He wants the stone left in the bog for ever: the council will make the place of the light a monument, with a fence and a keeper. Do not fish it out, "for the good of all".

Firmi. Il sindaco ti paga in contanti, n.easy: You sign. The mayor pays you in cash, with new banknotes that still smell of ink. That same evening he takes the stone to the dyke with the whole council and throws it into the bog in front of everyone. When it sinks, all the people on the dyke sigh at the same time, like someone putting down something heavy.
Firmi. Il sindaco ti paga in contanti, n.short: You sign, and are paid in crisp new notes. That evening the mayor throws the stone into the bog before the whole council. As it sinks, the crowd sighs as one, as if setting down a weight.

Gli dai la tua parola, e lui ti stringe.easy: You give him your word, and he shakes your hand for a long time. His hand is cold, but he means it. "I knew I could trust you," he says. "You are people from here."
Gli dai la tua parola, e lui ti stringe.short: You give your word. His handshake is cold, but sincere. "I knew I could trust you. You are people from here."

Il sindaco non si offende. Non si offend.easy: The mayor is not offended. In {0} nobody is ever offended. He carefully puts the contract back in the drawer and walks with you to the door. "The council has time," he says. "Much more time than you."
Il sindaco non si offende. Non si offend.short: The mayor is not offended; nobody in {0} ever is. He puts the contract away. "The council has time. Much more than you."

Al Blacksmith, che ormai è un'officina m.easy: The Blacksmith is now a workshop for machines, with an electric lathe. Jaap Mol's grandson is keeping a box for the family of the estate. Inside are brass parts, copper wire and pieces of black glass. He says old Jaap ordered them before he died, "for when the Machine is needed". A man from the council is in the workshop too. He wants to buy the whole box, for any price. For the museum, he says.
Al Blacksmith, che ormai è un'officina m.short: Jaap Mol's grandson has a crate for the estate: brass, copper wire, black glass, ordered by old Jaap "for when the Machine is needed". A council gentleman offers any price for it. For the museum, he says.

Con questi pezzi, e con il segmento di r.easy: With these parts, and with the spare part that your family has kept in the cellar since it paid for it at the foundry, the ring would be complete.
Con questi pezzi, e con il segmento di r.short: With these and the spare segment in your cellar, the ring would be complete.

Il signore del consiglio si rivolge a te.easy: The man from the council turns to you with a smile. He knows the Machine is yours. He offers you twice as much if you forget about it.
Il signore del consiglio si rivolge a te.short: The council gentleman knows the Machine is yours. He offers double if you let it go.

Il signore del consiglio paga e fa caric.easy: The man from the council pays and has the box put on a cart. The cart goes along the dyke, not towards the museum. In the evening, from the tower, you see the box float on the bog for a moment, and then slowly sink.
Il signore del consiglio paga e fa caric.short: The cart with the crate takes the dyke road, not the museum's. That evening, from the tower, you watch the crate float a moment on the bog, then sink.

Porti la cassa nella torre e lavori tutt.easy: You take the box to the tower and work all night. Every part fits, as if it was made yesterday. Near dawn, for a moment, the ring hums: a low sound, like bees inside a wall. Then it is quiet.
Porti la cassa nella torre e lavori tutt.short: You work all night in the tower. Every part fits. Towards dawn the ring hums for an instant, like bees in a wall. Then silence.

Carichi la cassa sul tuo carro sotto gli.easy: You put the box on your cart while the man from the council watches. He says nothing. {0} is waiting for you at the tower, with hands dirty with grease, and hugs you.
Carichi la cassa sul tuo carro sotto gli.short: You load the crate as the council gentleman watches in silence. At the tower {0}, hands black with grease, embraces you.

All'University, nel laboratorio di fisio.easy: At the University, in a laboratory they have lent her, Wil Maas is measuring temperatures. She is thirty-three, with short hair and hands damaged by disinfectant. She smokes English cigarettes, one after the other. At the front, she says, she saw men come back from no man's land after three days in the mud, with cold hands and a calm smile. They stood in line for their food as if nothing had happened. The doctors called them "the lucky ones". She had a different name for them, and she did not write it down.
All'University, nel laboratorio di fisio.short: At the University Wil Maas, thirty-three, chain-smoking, measures temperatures. At the front she saw men come back from three days in the mud with cold hands and calm smiles. "The lucky ones," said the doctors. She called them something else.

Passi il pomeriggio con lei: un nome, un.easy: You spend the afternoon with her: a name, a thermometer, a number, the next person. In four hours there are three cold hands, all soldiers back from the war, all smiling. At the end Wil lights her last cigarette and asks if you dream at night. You say yes. She nods and writes the number on your wrist with her pen, "so you will remember it".
Passi il pomeriggio con lei: un nome, un.short: An afternoon of names and thermometers: three cold hands in four hours, all smiling soldiers. Wil asks if you still dream. You say yes. She writes your temperature on your wrist, "so you remember".

Wil tira fuori dal taschino l'orologio d.easy: Wil takes grandmother Hester's watch out of her pocket. It is old and worn, its glass is cracked, and your family's crest is on the lid. It has been stopped at a quarter past eleven since before she was born. "Grandmother said it was yours," she says. "She said your great-grandfather found it on the floor of the tower. My father said it was just one of her stories." She puts it back in her pocket. "I believe it."
Wil tira fuori dal taschino l'orologio d.short: Wil shows you Hester's cracked watch, your crest on the lid, stopped at a quarter past eleven. "Grandmother said your great-grandfather found it in the tower. My father called it one of her stories. I believe it."

Al cimitero sull'argine stanno montando.easy: At the cemetery on the dyke they are building the war memorial: a tall granite stone with an angel on top. Two names are carved on it: the two {0} boys who did not come back. But the stonemason has a problem, and he shows you. In March the council sent him a list of five names. Then, in June, it sent a new list with only two names. The council says the other three have come back. The stonemason saw them at the party. But he has also seen the telegrams from the ministry that said they were dead.
Al cimitero sull'argine stanno montando.short: The war memorial bears two names. But the council's list in March had five. The other three came back, says the council. The stonemason saw them at the party. He has also seen the telegrams reporting them dead.

Accanto al monumento c'è la tomba del vo.easy: Next to the memorial is your great-grandfather's grave, covered with Fokke Tammer's black peat. In fifty years not one blade of grass has grown on it.
Accanto al monumento c'è la tomba del vo.short: Beside it, your great-grandfather's grave under Fokke's black peat: not a blade of grass in fifty years.

Accanto al monumento c'è la tomba del vo.easy: Next to the memorial is your great-grandfather's grave. Its granite stone is leaning, as if something under it had pushed for fifty years and never got out.
Accanto al monumento c'è la tomba del vo.short: Beside it, your great-grandfather's tilted slab, as if something below had pushed for half a century.

Lo scalpellino ti dà il foglio. Tre nomi.easy: The stonemason gives you the paper. It has the names of three {0} boys. They went missing in the mud of Flanders in 1917, and they came home in 1919, healthy, without papers, with dry clothes. One of the three is Jan Hoek, Hendrik Tammer's cousin. Hendrik, Fokke's grandson, came back with the right papers and a wound in his shoulder.
Lo scalpellino ti dà il foglio. Tre nomi.short: Three boys missing in Flanders in 1917, home in 1919: healthy, no papers, dry clothes. One is Jan Hoek, Hendrik Tammer's cousin. Hendrik came back with papers in order and a wounded shoulder.

Lo scalpellino incide i cinque nomi, e i.easy: The stonemason carves the five names. On the day of the ceremony the mayor reads them all, without stopping, in the same voice. The three who "came back" are in the front row with their medals. They hear their own names on the memorial to the dead, and they do not move. Then they clap with everyone else.
Lo scalpellino incide i cinque nomi, e i.short: The stonemason carves all five. The mayor reads them out unhesitating. The three "returned", front row, hear their names among the dead without blinking, then applaud with the rest.

Al Technician, l'officina dove si ripara.easy: The Technician is the workshop where they repair dynamos and sell electrical things. The engineer from the electric company, a man from the city with a straw hat and a bow tie, is planning the new power line along the dyke. He has a problem. The tower of the estate is the highest point in the area, and the company wants to put an insulator on top. He has seen the brass ring from the road and asked what it is. Nobody in the village could tell him. He says nobody wanted to.
Al Technician, l'officina dove si ripara.short: The light company's engineer wants an insulator on the estate's tower, the highest point around. He saw the brass ring from the road and asked what it was. Nobody would tell him.

L'ingegnere accetta con entusiasmo. In u.easy: The engineer is happy to agree. In one week the tower has an insulator, a cable, a meter and a light bulb hanging over the brass ring. The first evening you turn it on, all the pieces of black glass shine for a moment, like an eye that opens and closes.
L'ingegnere accetta con entusiasmo. In u.short: Within a week a bulb hangs over the brass ring. The first evening you switch it on, the black glass lights up for an instant, like an eye opening and closing.

L'ingegnere alza le spalle e sposta la l.easy: The engineer shrugs and moves the line three hundred metres towards the bog. They put the new pole at the point closest to the light. Two weeks later the pole is leaning. After a month it is gone: the peat has swallowed it up to the top.
L'ingegnere alza le spalle e sposta la l.short: The line moves towards the bog, its pole planted near the place of the light. In two weeks it leans. In a month the peat has swallowed it whole.

Ti svegli nell'acqua della torbiera, in.easy: You wake up standing in the water of the bog, with the water up to your waist. It is dawn. You are not cold. You remember everything: your childhood, the war, the party, the name of every person you love. You are still you. But for the first time in your life, you feel at peace. Your hands are cold. Under you, in the peat, someone with your face is in a deep sleep. You do not wake that sleeping body. It looks so tired.
Ti svegli nell'acqua della torbiera, in.short: You wake at dawn waist-deep in the bog, not cold, remembering everything. You are still you, only at peace for the first time. Your hands are cold. Below you in the peat, someone with your face sleeps. You let them sleep.

Sogni la torbiera all'alba, immersa fino.easy: You dream that you are in the bog at dawn, with the water up to your waist. The water is as still as a mirror. Someone with your face comes out of the water, dry, and walks towards the village without looking back. You wake up suddenly in your bed, with sweat on your forehead and your heart beating fast. It was only a dream. Maybe the last dream you will ever have.
Sogni la torbiera all'alba, immersa fino.short: You dream that someone with your face climbs dry out of the bog and walks to the village without looking back. You wake sweating. Only a dream. Perhaps your last.

Dalla finestra si vede la torbiera, piat.easy: From the window you can see the bog, flat and grey under the morning sky. At the place where the light was, for a moment, the water moves.
Dalla finestra si vede la torbiera, piat.short: At the place of the light, under the grey dawn, the water ripples for a moment.

Il sonno arriva subito, profondo e senza.easy: You fall asleep at once, deeply, with no dreams. When you wake up, you feel stronger than you have felt for years.
Il sonno arriva subito, profondo e senza.short: You sleep at once, deep and dreamless, and wake stronger than in years.

Il mattino dopo la festa, {0} è più quie.easy: The morning after the party, {0} is quieter than usual. At the market people talk softly. At the café nobody reads the newspaper out loud. The children walk to school in a line and do not run. At the estate breakfast is at eight, as always. You all sit down at the table together and look at each other for a long time, without speaking. Then someone asks for the salt, and someone passes it.
Il mattino dopo la festa, {0} è più quie.short: The morning after, {0} is quieter than ever. At the estate's breakfast you all look at one another a long time in silence. Then someone asks for the salt, and someone passes it.

Ve li raccontate, uno dopo l'altro: l'ar.easy: You tell your dreams, one after the other: the dyke, the water up to the waist, someone with your face. The dreams are almost the same. Almost. When it is their turn, one of you tells a beautiful, peaceful dream, full of light. And everyone at the table stops eating.
Ve li raccontate, uno dopo l'altro: l'ar.short: You tell your dreams in turn: the dyke, the water, someone with your face. Almost the same. Then one of you tells a dream full of peace and light, and everyone stops eating.

Vi prendete le mani sopra la tovaglia, a.easy: You hold hands over the tablecloth in a circle, like people calling spirits. Nobody speaks. Some hands are warm, some are only a little warm: it is November, the stove is not working well, the coffee is cold. Nobody wants to let go first. When you finally let go, nobody has understood anything, and everyone is afraid.
Vi prendete le mani sopra la tovaglia, a.short: You join hands round the table like a séance. Some warm, some lukewarm: it is November, the coffee is cold. When you let go, nobody knows anything, and everyone is afraid.

Fate finta di niente. Parlate del tempo,.easy: You act as if nothing has happened. You talk about the weather, the party and the mayor's speech. It is a perfect breakfast, polite and calm, like the breakfasts of every family in {0}. At some point you all notice it, at the same moment.
Fate finta di niente. Parlate del tempo,.short: You talk about the weather and the party: a perfect, calm breakfast, like every family's in {0}. You all notice it at the same moment.

Chiamata alla torre della tenuta alle un.easy: At half past eleven at night {0} called me to the tower of the estate. They sounded like someone who did not know whether to laugh or cry.
Chiamata alla torre della tenuta alle un.short: Called to the estate's tower at half past eleven at night by {0}, torn between laughing and crying.

Racconto quello che mi è stato raccontat.easy: I write what I was told, and what I saw. For months {0} has been working on the great-grandfather's Machine, the brass ring at the top of the tower. This evening, to test it when it was only half repaired, they put on the platform the first thing in their pocket. It was the great-grandfather's silver pocket watch, the one with the family crest. In the family it goes to the person who keeps the Machine. Its glass cracked in the war, in a trench in Flanders. At a quarter past eleven the Machine turned on: white light, no heat, a hum like bees. The watch disappeared. It did not appear anywhere else: not on the bog, not in the garden, not in the village.
Racconto quello che mi è stato raccontat.short: Testing the half-repaired Machine tonight, {0} put great-grandfather's watch on the platform, its glass cracked in a Flanders trench. At a quarter past eleven: white light, a hum of bees. The watch vanished, and appeared nowhere.

Ho tirato fuori dal taschino l'orologio.easy: I took grandmother Hester's watch out of my pocket. We put it on the table, next to the empty platform. The same crest. The same scratch on the lid, shaped like a hook. The same crack in the glass, with the same small piece missing at the top left. Mine is just older: the silver is worn down to the copper, and the letters inside the lid are gone with the years. It has stopped at a quarter past eleven.
Ho tirato fuori dal taschino l'orologio.short: I put grandmother Hester's watch beside the empty platform. Same crest, same hook-shaped scratch, same crack, same missing chip. Mine is only older, worn to the copper. Stopped at a quarter past eleven.

È lo stesso orologio. Il bisnonno lo tro.easy: It is the same watch. The great-grandfather found it on the floor of the tower on the night of the two lights, in 1865, and gave it to my grandmother to pay her. It is the same watch that {0} sent away this evening.
È lo stesso orologio. Il bisnonno lo tro.short: It is the same watch. Great-grandfather found it in the tower on the night of the two lights, in 1865. {0} sent it away this evening.

**La Macchina non sposta le cose soltant.easy: **The Machine does not only move things from one place to another. It also moves them in time. And the other end of the line is the night of the two lights. That night the Machine did not turn on by itself: someone here, now, was using it. The stone came from the future.**
**La Macchina non sposta le cose soltant.short: **The Machine moves things in time as well. Its other end is the night of the two lights: that night someone, from here, was using it. The stone came from the future.**

Ho controllato il mio polso tre volte, c.easy: I checked my pulse three times, like my father did. It was normal. It was the only normal thing in the room.
Ho controllato il mio polso tre volte, c.short: I checked my pulse three times, like my father. Normal. The only normal thing in the room.

Decidete di dire tutto. Wil Maas vi guar.easy: You decide to tell everything. Wil Maas looks at you for a long time, then nods. "At least it will be written somewhere else, not only here." That night, for the first time in years, nobody at the estate can sleep. Outside, on the road, people walk past slowly and stop to look at the tower.
Decidete di dire tutto. Wil Maas vi guar.short: You will tell everything. "At least it will be written somewhere besides here," says Wil. That night nobody at the estate sleeps. People pass slowly on the road, stopping to look at the tower.

Decidete di tacere. Wil Maas chiude il R.easy: You decide to say nothing. Wil Maas closes the Register without a word, puts her grandmother's watch back in her pocket, and asks you only one thing: do not use the Machine until you are sure what you are doing. Nobody tells her that now it is too late to be sure.
Decidete di tacere. Wil Maas chiude il R.short: You keep quiet. Wil asks only that you not use the Machine until you are sure what you are doing. Nobody tells her it is too late to be sure.

I giornali parlano della Macchina. Qualc.easy: The newspapers are writing about the Machine. Someone in the village saw the light on the tower on 11 November, exactly one year after the armistice, and wrote about it. The Morning Liberal calls it "the lighthouse of science". The Conservative Report calls it "a provocation". Neither newspaper talks about the bog.
I giornali parlano della Macchina. Qualc.short: The papers have seen the light on the tower, a year to the day after the armistice. "The beacon of science," says the Morning Liberal; "a provocation," says the Conservative Report. Neither mentions the bog.

Nella redazione del Morning Liberal, due.easy: The Morning Liberal has two rooms above a printing shop. The editor, Siemens, is a young man with his sleeves rolled up and ink on his fingers. He wants an interview about the Machine, of course: the science that takes {0} into the future. But he has another idea too, and he says it quietly: a story about "the water", about the perfect health of the people, about the soldiers who came back without a scratch. He needs someone who will talk.
Nella redazione del Morning Liberal, due.short: Siemens, the young editor of the Morning Liberal, wants an interview about the Machine. And, more quietly, an investigation into "the water" and the soldiers back without a scratch. He needs someone who will talk.

Parli della Macchina per un'ora, e il di.easy: You talk about the Machine for an hour, and the editor fills a notebook. The article comes out on Sunday, on the front page, with a drawing of the tower. Nobody believes it. Everyone reads it. In the evening curious people gather under the tower and look up, waiting for the light.
Parli della Macchina per un'ora, e il di.short: The article runs on Sunday's front page. Nobody believes it; everybody reads it. In the evening a crowd gathers under the tower, waiting for the light.

Racconti tutto: le temperature, i nomi,.easy: You tell him everything: the temperatures, the names, Gerrit's dig, the three boys on the memorial. The editor writes without looking up. The story comes out in three parts. Before the third part, the printing shop closes because a machine breaks down. The next day the editor, Siemens, says hello to you in the street, friendly, with his hands in his pockets. He does not remember that he interviewed you.
Racconti tutto: le temperature, i nomi,.short: You tell him everything. The investigation runs in three parts, and then the press "breaks down". Next day Siemens greets you warmly in the street, hands in his pockets. He does not remember interviewing you.

Il Conservative Report ha la sede in un.easy: The Conservative Report is in a brick building with shiny windows. Its editor is Piet Brink, a grey-haired man who left the council to work "for the news". He welcomes you with tea and an offer: a special issue about your family, "who have given so much to {0}". A picture of each of you, the story of your lives, a page about the tower. He only asks you to tell the right story: the tower is just a tower, the bog is just a bog, and {1} is a happy village.
Il Conservative Report ha la sede in un.short: Piet Brink, grey-haired editor of the Conservative Report, offers a special issue on your family. He asks only the right version: the tower is a tower, the bog is a bog, {0} is happy.

Il numero speciale esce con le vostre fa.easy: The special issue comes out with your faces on the front page. The photographer has changed the pictures so you look healthier than you are. In the village everyone asks you to sign a copy. They keep it on the table in the sitting room, next to the jug of water.
Il numero speciale esce con le vostre fa.short: The issue prints your faces retouched to look healthier than you are. Everyone has you sign it, and keeps it beside the water jug.

Piet Brink sorride, gentile, come sempre.easy: Piet Brink smiles kindly, as always. His mother died alone in the city, many years ago. He wrote to her every week. "I think she never forgave me for growing up," he says. Then he is quiet for a moment, and he adds softly, in a voice you have never heard before: "Sometimes, at night, I hear her calling. From down there."
Piet Brink sorride, gentile, come sempre.short: His mother died alone in the city, Piet smiles. "She never forgave me for growing up." Then, in a voice you do not know: "Sometimes, at night, I hear her calling. From down there."

Al General Store, tra i barattoli e le p.easy: At the General Store, among the jars and the shovels, they sell rubber boots that come up to your chest, for the peat-cutters. The shop assistant watches you take a pair and says nothing. The stone is in the bog, at the place where the light was, half a mile away. There is no fence and no guard.
Al General Store, tra i barattoli e le p.short: At the General Store you buy chest-high rubber boots. The assistant says nothing. The stone lies half a mile away in the bog. No fence, no keeper.

Al General Store il commesso, un giovane.easy: At the General Store the shop assistant, a young man with clean hands, wraps your parcel. While he does it, he kindly asks where you keep the stone at the estate. He says he is just curious. Everyone in the village wants to know.
Al General Store il commesso, un giovane.short: Wrapping your parcel, the clean-handed assistant asks kindly where the estate keeps the stone. Just curious. Everyone wonders.

Entri nella torbiera all'alba, con gli s.easy: At dawn you walk into the bog with the boots and a rope, to the place where the light was. The water is ice cold. The stone is down there, at the bottom, where they left it: warm, smooth, alive under your fingers. When you pull it out, ten people from the village are already standing on the dyke, a hundred steps away. They watch you come back to the bank in silence.
Entri nella torbiera all'alba, con gli s.short: At dawn you wade out and find the stone, warm and alive. As you pull it out, ten villagers are already on the dyke, silently watching you come back.

Glielo dici: nella cassa di ferro, nel l.easy: You tell him: in the iron box, in the laboratory. The shop assistant thanks you. The next night nobody hears anything, and nobody breaks a lock. In the morning the box is open and empty, and from the window you see the bog smoking.
Glielo dici: nella cassa di ferro, nel l.short: You tell him: the iron box in the laboratory. That night nobody hears a thing. By morning the box is open and empty, and the bog is smoking.

Esci con il pacco sotto il braccio e la.easy: You leave with the parcel under your arm. You feel that someone was watching you the whole time, and already knew the answer.
Esci con il pacco sotto il braccio e la.short: You leave feeling that someone watched you all along, already knowing the answer.

Al Laborer's Union, dove si assumono i r.easy: At the Laborer's Union, where soldiers back from the war are hired to work on the dyke, there is Hendrik Tammer, Fokke's grandson and Gerrit's son. He is thirty. He has a wound in his shoulder and the eyes of a man who has not slept for months. He is the only soldier who did not drink at the fountain. He says he does not sleep because he is afraid to fall asleep near the water. In the trenches he slept in the mud. In {0} he cannot sleep any more.
Al Laborer's Union, dove si assumono i r.short: Hendrik Tammer, Gerrit's son, thirty, wounded, sleepless, is the only soldier who did not drink at the fountain. He slept in the mud of the trenches. In {0} he is afraid to fall asleep near the water.

Suo nonno Fokke, quello vero, quello sve.easy: His grandfather Fokke, the real one, the one they woke up from the peat, died two years ago. He was drunk and happy, and he was shouting at the neighbours. Hendrik loved him.
Suo nonno Fokke, quello vero, quello sve.short: His real grandfather Fokke, woken from the peat, died two years ago, drunk, happy, cursing the neighbours. Hendrik loved him.

Suo nonno Fokke, quello vero, dorme anco.easy: His grandfather Fokke, the real one, is still sleeping under the peat in the Park. His father Gerrit made him promise never to let anyone take Fokke out unless Gerrit is there.
Suo nonno Fokke, quello vero, dorme anco.short: His real grandfather still sleeps under the Park. Gerrit made him promise never to let them dig Fokke out without him.

Hendrik entra nella Ronda come si entra.easy: Hendrik joins the Watch like a soldier going into a trench: without talking, checking his gun. From that night the Watch has a man who does not sleep and who can shoot. On the first night, on the dyke, he does not move for six hours. He watches the bog. At dawn he says only: "They are moving."
Hendrik entra nella Ronda come si entra.short: Hendrik joins the Watch like a man entering a trench. The first night he watches the bog for six hours without moving. At dawn he says only: "They are moving."

Wil Maas gli dà delle gocce per dormire.easy: Wil Maas gives him some drops to help him sleep, and some advice: sleep far from the water, upstairs, with the window closed. Hendrik thanks her. For the first time in months he sleeps for fourteen hours. When he wakes up, his hands are warm. He checks them for an hour.
Wil Maas gli dà delle gocce per dormire.short: Wil gives him sleeping drops: sleep upstairs, far from water. He sleeps fourteen hours. When he wakes his hands are warm. He checks them for an hour.

Alla Library, al bancone dei prestiti, c.easy: At the Library, at the desk, the new librarian, who is perfect, says hello to you by name. At the back of the room, in the armchair by the stove, sits Miss Neeltje Borg. She stopped teaching last year. She has a pile of notebooks on her knees. They are her pupils' dream diaries, from 1891 to 1918: almost thirty years of Mondays. She has kept them all. She wants to give them to someone before the new librarian puts them "in order".
Alla Library, al bancone dei prestiti, c.short: By the Library stove sits Miss Borg, retired, with her pupils' dream diaries from 1891 to 1918. She wants to give them to someone before the perfect new librarian puts them "in order".

Li porti alla tenuta e li sfogli la sera.easy: You take them to the estate and look through them in the evening, one by one. Every year there are more empty pages. In the last notebook, from 1918, there is only one drawing. A child has drawn himself twice, side by side: one in colour and one in black. Under it, in the crooked writing of a six-year-old: *me and me*.
Li porti alla tenuta e li sfogli la sera.short: Year by year the blank sheets multiply. In the 1918 book there is one drawing: a child drawn twice, side by side, once in colour, once in black. Below: *me and me*.

Neeltje ride, piano. Sogna ogni notte, d.easy: Neeltje laughs softly. She says she dreams every night: bad, confused dreams, full of people who are gone. She wakes up tired, with a headache. She is the happiest person in {0}. "The day I stop dreaming," she says, "come and check my hands."
Neeltje ride, piano. Sogna ogni notte, d.short: Neeltje laughs. She has bad dreams every night and wakes with a headache: the happiest woman in {0}. "The day I stop dreaming, come and check my hands."

Il paese dorme. Tu no: non ne hai più bi.easy: The village is sleeping. You are not: you do not need to sleep any more. You walk through the dark streets with your hands in your pockets, and from every window someone softly says hello. There are many of them, but not enough. Choose a house tonight. Tomorrow someone happier will live there.
Il paese dorme. Tu no: non ne hai più bi.short: The village sleeps; you no longer need to. From every dark window someone greets you softly. Many, but not enough. Choose a house tonight. Tomorrow someone happier will live there.

Il paese dorme. Tu quasi. Fuori, sulla s.easy: The village is sleeping. You are almost asleep. Outside on the road someone is walking slowly and calmly. They stop in front of a house. Then they walk on and stop in front of another one. Before you fall asleep, you try to understand where.
Il paese dorme. Tu quasi. Fuori, sulla s.short: Half asleep, you hear slow, calm steps outside stop at one house, then another. Before sleep takes you, you try to tell where.

Al mattino, in una casa del paese, qualc.easy: In the morning, in a house in the village, someone wakes up calmer than usual. They eat breakfast in silence and walk out of the house slowly, with their hands in their pockets. Nobody notices. Almost nobody.
Al mattino, in una casa del paese, qualc.short: In the morning, somewhere in the village, someone wakes more serene than usual and walks out, hands in pockets. Almost nobody notices.

Chiamata al Farmer's Market alle nove di.easy: They called me to the Farmer's Market at nine in the morning. Fokke Tammer, ninety-three years old on paper, was serving a customer when he stopped talking in the middle of a sentence. He stood still, with the change in his hand. Then the skin on his face became dry, like paper in the sun, and it cracked. In less than an hour, in front of a hundred people, Fokke Tammer fell apart into peat, from his head to his feet, like a brick left too long on the stove. When I arrived, on the stones of the street there was a pile of black peat, an apron and the coins of the change.
Chiamata al Farmer's Market alle nove di.short: Called to the market at nine. Fokke Tammer, ninety-three, stopped mid-sentence, the change in his hand. His face dried and cracked like paper, and within an hour he crumbled into peat before a hundred people. I found black peat, an apron, and the coins.

Nessuno gridava. La gente guardava. Poi,.easy: Nobody screamed. People watched. Then, one after the other, they looked at their own hands.
Nessuno gridava. La gente guardava. Poi,.short: Nobody screamed. Then, one by one, they looked at their hands.

**Dopo cinquantaquattro anni il corpo di.easy: **After fifty-four years the peat body cannot last any longer. The Neighbours do not live for ever, and they know it. The oldest ones are in a hurry to find new bodies.**
**Dopo cinquantaquattro anni il corpo di.short: **After fifty-four years the peat body gives out. The Neighbours do not last for ever, and the oldest are in a hurry.**

Gerrit Tammer, ormai vecchio, è venuto a.easy: Gerrit Tammer, who is old now, came to the market with his walking stick. He looked at the peat for a long time, then took off his hat. It was the man who brought him up.
Gerrit Tammer, ormai vecchio, è venuto a.short: Old Gerrit Tammer came with his stick, looked long at the peat, and took off his hat. It was the man who raised him.

Gerrit Tammer, ormai vecchio, è venuto a.easy: Gerrit Tammer, who is old now, came to the market with his walking stick. He picked up a handful of peat in a handkerchief and went to the Park, to the dig, where his real father is still sleeping. He put the peat on top of him.
Gerrit Tammer, ormai vecchio, è venuto a.short: Old Gerrit gathered a handful of the peat and scattered it over the dig in the Park, where his father still sleeps.

Il consiglio ha decretato il coprifuoco,.easy: After Fokke Tammer's death the council has ordered a curfew, "to be careful". Nobody may go out after ten o'clock. At night, in the streets of {0}, the only people walking are the ones who do not need to sleep. And there are many of them.
Il consiglio ha decretato il coprifuoco,.short: After Fokke's death the council imposes a curfew. At night only those who need no sleep walk {0}'s streets. There are many.

Dopo il test di Wil Maas, la voce ha fat.easy: After Wil Maas's test, the news went around the village in one hour. But nobody talks about it. In the morning, at the estate, the milkman leaves one more bottle than usual.
Dopo il test di Wil Maas, la voce ha fat.short: News of Wil's test went round the village in an hour. Nobody mentions it. The milkman leaves the estate an extra bottle.

Dopo l'articolo del Morning Liberal, sot.easy: Since the article in the Morning Liberal, curious people come under the tower every evening, and every evening there are more. They look up, in silence, and wait for the light.
Dopo l'articolo del Morning Liberal, sot.short: Every evening, more of the curious gather under the tower, silently waiting for the light.

Al cimitero, di notte, durante il coprif.easy: At night, during the curfew, the Watch found the grave of Jaap Mol, the smith, open. Nobody broke into it. It was opened from the inside. The earth is pushed up and to one side, like a blanket pushed away. The coffin is empty, except for a little peat. On paper, Jaap Mol died in 1915. But in 1915, Hendrik reminds you, the Jaap of the village was already almost fifty years old in peat. So who was buried here?
Al cimitero, di notte, durante il coprif.short: The Watch found Jaap Mol's grave opened from inside, the earth thrown back like a blanket, the coffin empty but for peat. Jaap was buried in 1915. But by then the village's Jaap was nearly fifty years of peat. Who was buried, then?

Wil esamina la torba della cassa con la.easy: Wil kneels on the loose earth and looks at the peat in the coffin with her lens. She says it has the shape of a man, but not of a dead man. It is the shape of a man who stood up. The Jaap buried in 1915 was the real one. Someone took him out of the canal and put him here to sleep. And tonight he woke up by himself.
Wil esamina la torba della cassa con la.short: The peat holds the shape of a man, says Wil, not dead but risen. The Jaap buried in 1915 was the real one, taken from the canal and laid here. Tonight he woke on his own.

Richiudete la tomba con le vanghe della.easy: In silence you close the grave with the spades of the Watch and put the flowers back on top. Nobody in the village will ever ask you about it. But the next morning, on the dyke, there are the footprints of a man with bare feet. They go from the cemetery to the bog, and they do not come back.
Richiudete la tomba con le vanghe della.short: You close the grave in silence. Nobody will ever ask. But next morning a barefoot man's prints lead from the cemetery to the bog, and do not come back.

In chiesa, la domenica, Trijntje Kalf su.easy: In church on Sunday, Trijntje Kalf plays the organ for only a few people: about twenty, in the front benches, old people, children and a few soldiers back from the war. There is no choir now. She tells you the others go to the bog on Sunday mornings, in a line. They stand on the dyke with water up to their ankles, in silence, for an hour. It is their church service. In the middle of the hymn, as her father asked before he died, Trijntje plays a wrong note, loudly. In the front benches someone smiles.
In chiesa, la domenica, Trijntje Kalf su.short: On Sunday Trijntje plays for twenty people. The rest stand in silence at the bog, ankle-deep: their Mass. Mid-hymn she plays her loud wrong note. Someone in the front pews smiles.

Resti. Canti male, fuori tempo, con la v.easy: You stay. You sing badly, at the wrong speed, and your voice breaks. Next to you an old peat-cutter sings even worse, and pushes you with his elbow, laughing. Trijntje plays another wrong note, and another. At the end, nobody sits down at the same moment.
Resti. Canti male, fuori tempo, con la v.short: You stay and sing badly. An old peat-cutter sings worse and nudges you, laughing. Trijntje plays wrong note after wrong note. At the end nobody sits down at the same moment.

All'argine ci sono trecento persone, in.easy: At the dyke there are three hundred people in a line, with water up to their ankles, hands by their sides and eyes closed. Nobody speaks. Nobody moves. It is so quiet that you can hear the sleepers breathing under the peat, hundreds of them. For a moment you want to take off your shoes and stand in the line too.
All'argine ci sono trecento persone, in.short: Three hundred people stand ankle-deep at the dyke, eyes closed. In the silence you hear hundreds of sleepers breathing beneath the peat. For a moment you want to take off your shoes and join them.

Al General Store, sul retro, c'è il maga.easy: At the back of the General Store there is the storeroom for the bottles of "{0} Water", with the label. The village has sold it all over the province for thirty years. The owner, a calm man with a white apron, shows you the latest order. A city in the south wants ten thousand bottles, for the hospitals for soldiers. Against bad dreams, he says. The council has already said yes. They only need transport, and the estate's carts are the biggest in the village.
Al General Store, sul retro, c'è il maga.short: A southern city has ordered ten thousand bottles of {0} Water, for the soldiers' hospitals, against nightmares. The council has approved. They need only carts, and the estate's are the biggest.

I carri partono all'alba, carichi fino a.easy: The carts leave at dawn for the station, full to the top. The owner pays you well and thanks you for the village. The next month you read in the newspaper that in the southern hospitals the soldiers' bad dreams have gone. No more screaming at night, no more attacks, no more running away. The doctors call it a miracle. The patients do not talk much any more.
I carri partono all'alba, carichi fino a.short: The carts leave at dawn. A month later the paper reports the southern hospitals' nightmares gone: no screams, no fits. The doctors speak of a miracle. The patients hardly speak at all.

Entri nel magazzino con un bastone e rom.easy: You go into the storeroom with a stick and break everything you can before someone stops you. Nobody stops you. The owner watches with his hands in his pockets, while the dark water spreads over the floor and runs under the door, towards the road and towards the dyke. When you finish, he gives you a towel.
Entri nel magazzino con un bastone e rom.short: You smash every bottle you can. Nobody stops you. The owner watches, hands in pockets, as the water runs under the door towards the dyke. Then he offers you a towel.

Al Farmer's Market, il banco della torba.easy: At the Farmer's Market the black peat stall is empty, under a sheet. Fokke's pile of peat was swept away the same day. But on the stones where he fell there is a darker shape, like a man, and nobody walks on it. There are flowers in front of the stall. And there is a line of people, waiting in silence. They tell you they are waiting for the new peat-cutter. One will come, they say. One always comes.
Al Farmer's Market, il banco della torba.short: Fokke's stall stands empty under a sheet. A man-shaped stain darkens the cobbles. A silent queue waits in front: for the new peat-cutter. One always comes, they say.

Ti rispondono con dolcezza, uno dopo l'a.easy: They answer you kindly, one after the other, the way you answer a child. Someone who loves peat, who is good with their hands, who works hard. Someone from Fokke's family, maybe. Hendrik, for example, who never sleeps. They say it with love, and with a patient waiting that makes you go cold.
Ti rispondono con dolcezza, uno dopo l'a.short: Someone who loves the peat and works hard, they answer gently. From Fokke's family, perhaps. Hendrik, who never sleeps. Their patient affection chills you.

Togli il telo e ti metti dietro il banco.easy: You take off the sheet and stand behind the stall, with your hands on Fokke's black peat. The line moves, and the first customer asks you for two bricks, with a smile. You sell all day. In the evening your hands are black up to the wrists, and the smell of the bog does not go away with soap. But your hands are warm.
Togli il telo e ti metti dietro il banco.short: You stand behind the stall and sell Fokke's peat all day. By evening your hands are black to the wrists and smell of the bog. But they are warm.

Nello studio del Town Hall, Wil Maas pre.easy: In her room at the Town Hall, Wil Maas gets ready a thermometer, a lens and a needle that she cleans in the flame of the lamp. "Red blood: healthy," she says. "Dark water: not. I do not make mistakes. I have not made a mistake for four years." She asks who she must examine.
Nello studio del Town Hall, Wil Maas pre.short: Wil Maas readies a thermometer, a lens and a flame-sterilised needle. "Red blood, healthy. Dark water, not. I have not been wrong in four years." Whom is she to examine?

L'ago entra nel polpastrello, senza dolo.easy: The needle goes into the fingertip, without pain. A thick black drop comes out. It smells of smoke. Wil Maas says nothing. She looks at the drop, then at {0}, for a long time, with no fear and no hate. Then, gently, she takes {1}'s hand in hers and holds it, like you hold the hand of a sick person in bed. It is cold.
L'ago entra nel polpastrello, senza dolo.short: A thick black drop, smelling of smoke. Wil looks long at {0}, without fear or hatred, then holds {1}'s hand as at a sickbed. It is cold.

L'ago entra nel polpastrello, e {0} tras.easy: The needle goes into the fingertip, and {0} jumps. A red drop comes out, alive. Wil Maas looks at it, cleans it with cotton, and smiles for the first time since she came back. "Thirty-six point eight," she says. "The blood of a living person."
L'ago entra nel polpastrello, e {0} tras.short: {0} flinches at the needle. A red, living drop. Wil smiles for the first time since she came back. "Thirty-six point eight. Living blood."

Tutti sanno che cosa sei. Nessuno te l'h.easy: Everyone knows what you are. Nobody has blamed you for it. The family treats you with a kindness you never knew before, like a sick person. But at night, from the window, you hear the bog calling you softly, with your own voice. Down there, under the peat, someone with your face has been sleeping in the cold for weeks. You could go back and let them wake up. Or you could stay, and live in their place for fifty years, in peace.
Tutti sanno che cosa sei. Nessuno te l'h.short: Everyone knows what you are, and treats you kindly, like an invalid. At night the bog calls you in your own voice. Under the peat someone with your face sleeps in the cold. Go back and let them wake, or stay and live fifty peaceful years in their place.

Il 31 dicembre 1919, alle undici di sera.easy: On 31 December 1919, at eleven at night, the family is together at the top of the tower, around the brass ring. Outside it is snowing on the bog, but at the place where the light was the snow does not stay. Wil Maas has come up with the Register under her arm and her grandmother's watch in her pocket. She puts the watch on the table, open. It has stopped at a quarter past eleven. From the windows you can see the village, completely dark. Nobody in {0} is sleeping tonight.
Il 31 dicembre 1919, alle undici di sera.short: 31 December 1919, eleven at night. The family gathers round the brass ring. Snow falls on the bog, but not on the place of the light. Wil lays Hester's watch on the table, at a quarter past eleven. The village is dark. Nobody in {0} sleeps tonight.

Uno dei certificati, sul tavolo, mostra.easy: One of the certificates on the table shows the side with no crown. There is a long silence. Then the person who turned it smiles calmly and holds out their hands to the fire, though they do not need to warm them.
Uno dei certificati, sul tavolo, mostra.short: One certificate shows no crown. A long silence. Then its owner smiles calmly and holds their hands to the fire, with no need of the warmth.

Tutti i certificati mostrano la corona..easy: All the certificates show the crown. None of you has changed. You look at each other, and someone laughs with relief, too loudly. "For now," says Wil Maas.
Tutti i certificati mostrano la corona..short: Every certificate shows the crown. Someone laughs with relief, too loudly. "For now," says Wil.

{0} abbassa la leva. L'anello d'ottone s.easy: {0} pulls the lever down. The brass ring lights up with a white light, with no heat, and starts to hum. It is a deep, regular hum, like breathing. On the platform, in the middle, there is space for only one thing, as big as a loaf of bread.
{0} abbassa la leva. L'anello d'ottone s.short: {0} pulls the lever. The ring lights white and hums like breathing. On the platform there is room for one thing, the size of a loaf.

{0} abbassa la leva. L'anello d'ottone t.easy: {0} pulls the lever down. The brass ring flickers, hums for a moment, and goes dark. Something is still missing. There is no time left.
{0} abbassa la leva. L'anello d'ottone t.short: {0} pulls the lever. The ring flickers, hums an instant, and dies. Something is missing. There is no time left.

Prima che la votazione cominci, {0} si a.easy: Before the vote starts, {0} stands up, puts on a coat and goes down the stairs of the tower without looking back. Nobody tries to stop them. From the window you follow the footprints in the snow, towards the bog, to the place where the light was, to the black water, and into it, slowly, until there is nothing left.
Prima che la votazione cominci, {0} si a.short: Before the vote, {0} puts on a coat and goes down the tower stairs without looking back. Nobody stops them. From the window you follow the footprints in the snow to the black water, and into it, until nothing is left.

La Macchina è accesa. La pietra è sul ta.easy: The Machine is on. The stone is on the table, warm, next to Wil's watch. The great-grandfather wrote it: *it must go back where it came from*. Now you know where it came from: from the other end of the line, from the night of the two lights. You only need to put it on the platform. Or there is Jaap Mol's hammer on the workbench. With one exact blow, you can break the stone.
La Macchina è accesa. La pietra è sul ta.short: The Machine is on, the warm stone beside Wil's watch. *It must go back where it came from*: to the night of the two lights. Put it on the platform. Or take Jaap Mol's hammer, and break it with one precise blow.

La Macchina tace. La pietra è sul tavolo.easy: The Machine is quiet. The stone is on the table, warm, next to Wil's watch. There are two ways left, and neither of them sends it back where it came from. Jaap Mol's hammer on the workbench, with one exact blow. Or the dyke, the bog, the place where the light was, where the whole village has waited for it for fifty years.
La Macchina tace. La pietra è sul tavolo.short: The Machine is silent. Two roads remain, neither of them home for the stone: Jaap Mol's hammer, or the place of the light, where the whole village has waited fifty years.

La pietra è nella torbiera, lontana, sot.easy: The stone is in the bog, far away, under the snow that does not stay. You will not get to it tonight. But under the peat, hundreds of the real people are sleeping: Fokke, the miller's wife, Mrs Mulder, the boys on the memorial. Gerrit Tammer has left the spades from the dig at the estate, with a note: *If you want, it can be done.* You can wake them all tonight. Or you can let them sleep, and close the Register.
La pietra è nella torbiera, lontana, sot.short: The stone is out of reach tonight. But hundreds of originals sleep under the peat. Gerrit has left his spades with a note: *If you want, it can be done.* Wake them all, or let them sleep and close the Register.

**UNA LUCE SULLA TORRE.** L'altro ieri,.easy: **A LIGHT ON THE TOWER.** Two days ago, at a quarter past eleven at night, exactly one year after the armistice, many people saw a very bright white light for a moment at the top of the tower of the estate. There was no noise and no smoke. This newspaper asked the family of the estate about it. They said it was "scientific experiments".
**UNA LUCE SULLA TORRE.** L'altro ieri,.short: **A LIGHT ON THE TOWER.** On the armistice's anniversary, at a quarter past eleven at night, many saw a blinding white light flash atop the estate's tower. The family speaks of "scientific experiments".

Uno degli eredi ha aggiunto, con nostra.easy: To our surprise, one of the heirs added something more. We print it all here, and our readers can judge: "Our great-grandfather's machine moves things in time. The stone from the bog comes from the future. Stop drinking that water." We only point out that in {0} nobody has been ill for fifty years.
Uno degli eredi ha aggiunto, con nostra.short: One heir added: "Our great-grandfather's machine moves things in time. The stone comes from the future. Stop drinking that water." We note only that nobody in {0} has been ill for fifty years.

Gli eredi non hanno voluto aggiungere al.easy: The heirs did not want to say more. Dr Maas, who was at the tower, only said that "everyone is well". To the writer of this article, her voice did not sound reassuring at all.
Gli eredi non hanno voluto aggiungere al.short: The heirs would say no more. Dr Maas said only that "everyone is well", in a tone far from reassuring.

**BRUNVEEN NON HA BISOGNO DI SPETTACOLI..easy: **BRUNVEEN DOES NOT NEED A SHOW.** Our village is the healthiest, the tidiest and the quietest in the province. It does not need lights on towers or strange ideas. We ask the family of the estate to remember that peace belongs to everyone, and that the council has already offered every kind of help to keep it.
**BRUNVEEN NON HA BISOGNO DI SPETTACOLI..short: **BRUNVEEN HAS NO NEED OF SPECTACLES.** The healthiest, quietest village in the province needs no lights on towers. Peace is a common good: the family of the estate would do well to remember it.

Alla Traveling Caravan, fra i carri dell.easy: At the Traveling Caravan, among the carts of the autumn fair, there is a tent with a painted sign: WONDERS OF SCIENCE – TRAVELLING SHOW OF THE NATURAL HISTORY MUSEUM. Inside, in glass cases, there is a mammoth's tooth, a calf with two heads that was never born, and a piece of a meteorite. At the back, in a case by itself, there is a little velvet box, open.
Alla Traveling Caravan, fra i carri dell.short: At the autumn fair, the city museum's travelling exhibition: a mammoth's tooth, a two-headed calf, a meteorite. At the back, alone in its case, an open velvet box.

Nella scatolina c'è la scheggia della pi.easy: In the little box there is the chip of the stone that your family sold to Professor Ostrander many years ago. It is in a glass of water, because "if it stays dry it gets too hot", the attendant explains. The attendant is an old, calm man with cold hands. He is the same man who worked at the museum when Ostrander was there. He has not got much older.
Nella scatolina c'è la scheggia della pi.short: In it, in a glass of water, lies the chip your family sold to Ostrander: "dry, it gets too hot". The attendant, calm, cold-handed, worked at the museum in Ostrander's day. He has hardly aged.

Nella scatolina non c'è niente. Il carte.easy: The little box is empty. The label says: *Stone of the light, {0}. Not acquired.* Next to it, in a frame, there is a page from the diary of Professor Ostrander, who died years ago: *I asked the family for a chip and they said no. Bless them. The city has enough troubles already.*
Nella scatolina non c'è niente. Il carte.short: The box is empty: *Stone of the light, {0}. Not acquired.* Beside it, a page of Ostrander's diary: *The family refused me a chip. Bless them. The city is ill enough already.*

Il custode accetta il denaro senza discu.easy: The attendant takes the money without arguing, as if he was waiting for you. He gives you the little box with the glass, and tells you never to let it get dry. At home the chip moves by itself to the edge of the glass, on the side towards the tower. When you take it into the tower, next to the ring, it stops moving.
Il custode accetta il denaro senza discu.short: The attendant sells it as if he expected you. At home the chip creeps to the side of the glass facing the tower. Beside the ring, it lies still.

Rompi la teca con il gomito. L'acqua si.easy: You break the glass with your elbow. The water spills, and on the wooden floor of the tent the chip starts to smoke. In a few seconds it burns a hole in the floor and disappears into the ground. The attendant does not shout. He looks at the hole, then at you, with pale, patient eyes. "It will go home," he says. "They all go home."
Rompi la teca con il gomito. L'acqua si.short: You smash the case. Out of the water the chip smokes, burns through the floor and vanishes into the earth. The attendant looks at you patiently. "It will go home. They all go home."

Il diario è aperto su un'altra pagina, p.easy: The diary is open at another page, later on, written by a shaking hand: *I brought a little bottle of {0} water to the museum, to study it. The attendant drank a sip, for a bet. The attendant got better. The attendant's wife got better. We never studied it: we drank it all and ordered more. I have sold my beer and I drink water. I have never felt so calm. The only thing that frightens me is the idea that soon it will not frighten me any more.*
Il diario è aperto su un'altra pagina, p.short: A later page, in a shaking hand: *I brought {0} water to the museum. The attendant drank some for a bet, and was cured. We never analysed it: we drank it and ordered more. I have never been so serene. I fear only that soon I will not fear it.*

Esci dal padiglione. Fuori, la fiera è p.easy: You leave the tent. Outside, the fair is full of people who are laughing. You count them, and you notice that they all laugh at the same moment.
Esci dal padiglione. Fuori, la fiera è p.short: Outside, the fair is full of laughter. Counting, you notice they all laugh at the same moment.

Alla Traveling Caravan, durante il copri.easy: At the Traveling Caravan, during the curfew, there is only one cart. It is painted blue, with old gold letters: STAR WATER – FROM BRUNVEEN. The seller is a small man with no top hat. His face is the same as fifty years ago, exactly the same. He is selling the last little bottles of green glass. He says it is his last fair. His hands are cracking, like Fokke's.
Alla Traveling Caravan, durante il copri.short: One blue cart remains: STAR WATER – FROM BRUNVEEN. The seller has the very face of fifty years ago. It is his last fair, he says. His hands are cracking, like Fokke's.

Quando ti vede ti riconosce, o riconosce.easy: When he sees you, he knows you, or he knows your family. "You followed me that night," he says. "I was in the water up to my knees. You saw me go in. But you did not see me come out: the one who came out was already me."
Quando ti vede ti riconosce, o riconosce.short: He knows your family. "You followed me that night. You saw me go into the water. But the one who came out was already me."

Quando ti vede ti riconosce, o riconosce.easy: When he sees you, he knows you, or he knows your family. "Mayor Wessel told me who reported me," he says kindly. "I was grateful to him. That evening, at the inn, I left behind everything I did not need any more."
Quando ti vede ti riconosce, o riconosce.short: He knows your family. "Mayor Wessel told me who reported me. I was grateful. At the inn I left behind everything I no longer needed."

La boccetta è fredda come il ghiaccio. I.easy: The little bottle is as cold as ice. The seller thanks you, closes his cart and walks away towards the dyke, leaving his horse tied up. The next morning, on the road, there is a pile of peat and a label drawn by hand: a star falling on a field.
La boccetta è fredda come il ghiaccio. I.short: The phial is ice cold. The seller walks off towards the dyke, leaving his horse. Next morning on the road: a heap of peat, and a label with a falling star.

Il venditore ci pensa, con la fronte agg.easy: The seller thinks, with a frown. He says he comes from here. He always has. Before, he was from another village, with another name, another wife and a top hat. Then he went into the water and woke up belonging here. "We are all from here," he says. "You too, now. You will see."
Il venditore ci pensa, con la fronte agg.short: He comes from here, he says, frowning. Before, he had another village, another name, a top hat. Then he went into the water. "We are all from here. You too, by now. You will see."

In chiesa si celebra il matrimonio di Ja.easy: In the church Jan Hoek, one of the three boys from the memorial, is marrying Marieke, the girl who waited four years for him. Jan came back in June, healthy and smiling, without papers. Before the ceremony Marieke stops you on the church steps, with her veil in her hand. In 1917 she got the telegram from the ministry: *missing*. Then Jan came back. He is kind and patient, and he has no bad dreams. He does not remember the song he used to sing to her under her window. Every day he asks her to marry him, with the same words.
In chiesa si celebra il matrimonio di Ja.short: Jan Hoek, back from Flanders without papers, is marrying Marieke. On the church steps she tells you: he is kind, patient, without nightmares. He has forgotten the song he sang under her window. He proposes every day, in the same words.

Marieke abbassa il velo ed entra in chie.easy: Marieke pulls down her veil and goes into the church. The wedding is perfect: nobody cries, nobody laughs, nobody says the wrong words. Outside, under the rice, Jan holds his wife's hand with his cold hand, and she smiles. A month later you see her at the market. She is calm and peaceful, with her hands in her pockets.
Marieke abbassa il velo ed entra in chie.short: Marieke lowers her veil and goes in. A perfect wedding. A month later you see her at the market: serene, hands in her pockets.

Marieke ti guarda a lungo, poi si toglie.easy: Marieke looks at you for a long time. Then she takes off her veil and goes home. The wedding is moved to a later date "because the bride is not well". Jan is not offended. Every morning, always on time, he brings her flowers, and he waits. He has all the time he wants.
Marieke ti guarda a lungo, poi si toglie.short: Marieke takes off her veil and goes home. The wedding is postponed. Jan brings her flowers every morning, and waits. He has all the time in the world.

All'altare, davanti a tutti, Marieke chi.easy: At the altar, in front of everyone, Marieke asks Jan to sing her the song from the window. Jan smiles kindly and sings. It is just a song, perfectly in tune, that nobody has ever heard. Marieke listens until the end. Then she says no, in front of the pastor, and runs out of the church with her veil in her hand. Jan stays at the altar, calm, and thanks everyone for coming.
All'altare, davanti a tutti, Marieke chi.short: At the altar Marieke asks for the window song. Jan sings, perfectly, a song nobody has ever heard. She says no and runs out. Jan stays, serene, and thanks everyone for coming.

In chiesa, alla funzione del giovedì, pr.easy: At the Thursday service the new pastor is preaching. He came after old Kalf died. He is a young man with fair hair and a warm, calm voice. His sermons are short and beautiful, with no threats. They talk about peace, about quiet, about the sleep of good people. The church is full.
