At the organ Trijntje Kalf plays her usual wrong note, and looks at him with hate. After the service the pastor comes up to you on the church steps. He has heard about the light on the tower. He would like to bless the Machine.
In chiesa, alla funzione del giovedì, pr.short: The fair-haired new pastor preaches peace, quiet and the sleep of the just to a full church. Trijntje plays her wrong note and glares at him. Afterwards he asks to bless the Machine.

Il pastore sale alla torre con l'acqua s.easy: The pastor climbs the tower with holy water and a book. In front of the brass ring he says a prayer you do not know. It is long and sweet, and it repeats itself. Then he throws drops of water on the ring. When the holy water touches the black glass, it hisses, like water on a hot stove. The pastor smiles, pleased, and leaves without looking back.
Il pastore sale alla torre con l'acqua s.short: Before the ring the pastor recites a long, sweet prayer you do not know. The holy water sizzles on the black glass like a stove. He smiles, satisfied, and leaves.

Il pastore ride: dal seminario della cit.easy: The pastor laughs: from the seminary in the city, of course. But when you ask the name of the seminary, he stops for just a moment before he says it. Trijntje was listening behind the door, and she takes you to one side. She wrote to that seminary. They answered that the pastor drowned two years ago, while he was skating on a bog near {0}.
Il pastore ride: dal seminario della cit.short: From the city seminary, he laughs, after the briefest pause over its name. Trijntje takes you aside: she wrote to them. The pastor drowned two years ago, skating on a bog near {0}.

Trijntje Kalf suonò l'organo della chies.easy: Trijntje Kalf played the organ in the {0} church every Sunday until she was eighty-five. Every Sunday, in the middle of the hymn, she played one wrong note, only one, loudly. When she died, the new organist played everything perfectly at her funeral. At the back of the church, someone stood up and walked out.
Trijntje Kalf suonò l'organo della chies.short: Trijntje Kalf played one loud wrong note every Sunday until she was eighty-five. At her funeral the new organist played perfectly. At the back, someone stood up and left.

La maestra Neeltje Borg sognò fino all'u.easy: Miss Neeltje Borg had dreams until the last night of her life. In the morning she wrote her last dream in her notebook, with a shaking hand: *the bog was dry, and there were children playing*. Then she went back to bed and never woke up. Her hands were warm.
La maestra Neeltje Borg sognò fino all'u.short: Miss Borg dreamed to the end. Her last dream, written with a trembling hand: *the bog was dry, and children were playing*. She went back to bed and did not wake. Her hands were warm.

Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.easy: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922 in the house on the dyke, with his son Hendrik next to him. On his bedside table there were two photographs: his father when young, with a spade on his shoulder, and his father when old, behind the black peat stall. He never said which one he loved more.
Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.short: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922 beside two photographs: his father young with his spade, and his father old at the peat stall. He never said which he loved more.

Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.easy: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922 in the house on the dyke, with his son Hendrik next to him. He had his father for two years: a peat-cutter of forty who drank and swore, called him "old man" and stole his tobacco. That was enough for him.
Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.short: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922. He had two years with his real father, a forty-year-old drunk who called him "old man" and stole his tobacco. It was enough.

Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.easy: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922 in the house on the dyke, with his son Hendrik next to him. After the fire he never went back to the Park. He said that at least his father died in his sleep.
Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.short: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922. After the fire he never went back to the Park. His father, he said, at least died sleeping.

Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.easy: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922 in the house on the dyke, with his son Hendrik next to him. Every Sunday, until the last one, he took flowers to the dig in the Park. His father is still sleeping there, under two metres of peat, with his hands together and the burns that never heal.
Gerrit Tammer morì nel 1922, nella casa.short: Gerrit Tammer died in 1922. Every Sunday he brought flowers to the dig, where his father still sleeps, hands folded, the burns unhealed.

La lanterna della Ronda, quella che il p.easy: The lantern of the Watch, the one Pastor Kalf lit first and {0} carried for years, hangs in the tower, next to the brass ring. Every evening someone lights it.
La lanterna della Ronda, quella che il p.short: The Watch's lantern, Pastor Kalf's and then {0}'s, hangs by the ring. Someone lights it every evening.

La vanga dei Tammer, quella che {0} pres.easy: The Tammer spade, the one {0} took from Gerrit's hands at the cemetery, hangs next to the lantern. Its handle is worn by three generations of warm hands.
La vanga dei Tammer, quella che {0} pres.short: Beside it hangs the Tammer spade {0} took from Gerrit, worn by three generations of warm hands.

Piet Brink, il direttore del Conservativ.easy: One winter evening Piet Brink, the editor of the Conservative Report, left the newspaper office without his coat and walked along the dyke. People saw him walk into the bog at the place where he fell as a boy, calling for his mother. He never came out. The next morning, on the bank, there was a fifteen-year-old boy, wet and barefoot, asking for the widow Brink.
Piet Brink, il direttore del Conservativ.short: One winter evening Piet Brink walked coatless into the bog where he fell as a boy, calling his mother. Next morning, on the bank, a wet, barefoot boy of fifteen was asking for the widow Brink.

I discendenti di Bruin, il cane di Fokke.easy: The great-grandchildren of Bruin, Fokke Tammer's dog, still live at the estate. They are black, big and patient. They only bark at some people. Nobody ever taught them to do it.
I discendenti di Bruin, il cane di Fokke.short: Bruin's descendants still live at the estate. They bark only at certain people. Nobody taught them.

La lampadina sopra l'anello d'ottone, qu.easy: The light bulb above the brass ring, from the electric company, has never burnt out. Since then the tower's electricity meter has turned backwards.
La lampadina sopra l'anello d'ottone, qu.short: The bulb above the ring has never burnt out. The tower's meter runs backwards.

Wil Maas visse fino a novant'anni e non.easy: Wil Maas lived until she was ninety, and she never married. Until the end, every evening before she slept, she took her grandmother's watch out of her pocket. It was stopped at a quarter past eleven. She wondered where the stone came from, if nobody sent it back. Then she put the watch away, took her temperature and wrote it down. Thirty-six point eight, always.
Wil Maas visse fino a novant'anni e non.short: Wil Maas lived to ninety, unmarried. Each night she looked at Hester's watch and wondered where the stone had come from, if nobody sent it back. Then she took her temperature. Thirty-six point eight, always.

Wil Maas visse fino a novant'anni e non.easy: Wil Maas lived until she was ninety, and she never married. Until the end, every evening before she slept, she took her temperature and wrote it down. Thirty-six point eight, always. She left her grandmother's watch to the family of the estate, with a note: *It was yours. It always has been.*
Wil Maas visse fino a novant'anni e non.short: Wil Maas lived to ninety, unmarried, taking her temperature every night: thirty-six point eight. She left Hester's watch to the estate: *It was yours. It always has been.*

Il quaderno del becchino Siebe, quello c.easy: Siebe the gravedigger's notebook, with the faces he saw in the water, went into the tower with the Register, or into the stove of his little house. Either way, nobody read it again. But the names are still down there.
Il quaderno del becchino Siebe, quello c.short: Siebe's notebook went into the tower or into the stove. Nobody read it again. The names are still down there.

Marieke, la ragazza che disse di no all'.easy: Marieke, the girl who said no at the altar, went to the city in 1920 and became an operetta singer. The critics say she sang out of tune in a beautiful way.
Marieke, la ragazza che disse di no all'.short: Marieke, who said no at the altar, became an operetta singer. She sang out of tune, the critics say, movingly.

Jan Hoek, il suo fidanzato tornato dalle.easy: Jan Hoek, her fiancé back from Flanders, never wrote to her. On the night of the stone, in his room, there was only a pile of peat and a pen.
Jan Hoek, il suo fidanzato tornato dalle.short: Jan Hoek never wrote to her: on the night of the stone, his room held only peat and a pen.

Jan e Marieke Hoek ebbero tre figli, san.easy: Jan and Marieke Hoek had three children. They were healthy, calm and very good at school. None of the three ever had a bad dream as a child.
Jan e Marieke Hoek ebbero tre figli, san.short: Jan and Marieke Hoek had three healthy, serene children. None of them ever had a nightmare.

Harm Visser, il mugnaio, morì a Rotterda.easy: Harm Visser, the miller, died in Rotterdam in 1901, poor, drunk and free. Every Christmas he sent a postcard to the estate, always with the same words: *Thank you for the ticket. Here we argue beautifully.*
Harm Visser, il mugnaio, morì a Rotterda.short: Harm Visser died in Rotterdam in 1901, poor, drunk and free. Every Christmas: *Thank you for the ticket. We quarrel beautifully here.*

Le catene di ferro che il capomastro Lam.easy: The iron chains that Lambert the master builder put around the tower are still there. They only rust on the side that faces the bog.
Le catene di ferro che il capomastro Lam.short: Lambert's chains still circle the tower. They rust only on the bog side.

Il ragazzo dei Van Dam, quello che sbagl.easy: The Van Dam boy, the one who did everything wrong, became the messiest mechanic in the province, and the most loved. When people asked him how he could make so many mistakes, he said that mistakes were the only way he knew to be sure he was still himself.
Il ragazzo dei Van Dam, quello che sbagl.short: Kees Van Dam became the province's messiest, best-loved mechanic. Mistakes, he said, were the only way he knew to be sure he was himself.

Non abbiamo votato. Mentre eravamo nella.easy: We did not vote. While we were in the tower, down in the village the Watch had already decided for everyone. Hendrik Tammer and about twenty men, the ones who never drank the water, went to the dyke with cans of paraffin from the electric company. At three in the morning they set fire to the bog in ten different places, all at the same time.
Non abbiamo votato. Mentre eravamo nella.short: We never voted. The Watch decided for everyone: at three in the morning Hendrik Tammer and twenty men who had never drunk set the bog alight in ten places at once.

La torba brucia in un modo che non si di.easy: Peat burns in a way you never forget. There are no high flames. It smokes and burns slowly, and it eats the ground from below, many metres deep. On top you see only a grey cloud and you smell something sweet. You cannot put it out. You cannot stop it. The firemen from the city came, looked and went away.
La torba brucia in un modo che non si di.short: Peat burns unforgettably: no flames, only smoke and a sweet smell, while it eats the earth from below. It cannot be stopped. The city firemen came, looked, and left.

La torbiera di {0} ha bruciato sotto ter.easy: The {0} bog burned under the ground for seven years. With everything that was inside it.
La torbiera di {0} ha bruciato sotto ter.short: The bog burned underground for seven years. With everything in it.

I Vicini non sono scappati. Sono andati.easy: The Neighbours did not run away. On the first morning they all went to the dyke together, in silence, and sat on the bank to watch the smoke, like people sitting with a dying relative. Many of them stayed there until they started to dry and crack, one by one, like Fokke. The others went back to the village, as kind as before. They never said a word to the people who lit the fire. For seven years they only said good morning to them.
I Vicini non sono scappati. Sono andati.short: The Neighbours did not run. They sat on the dyke watching the smoke like mourners. Many stayed until they dried and cracked, like Fokke. The rest went home, kind as ever, and for seven years wished the fire-setters good morning.

Io misuro ancora le temperature. Ma quan.easy: I still measure temperatures. But at night, when the wind brings the smell of burning peat into the village, I cannot sleep. I think of the people who were sleeping down there, and who did not wake up in time.
Io misuro ancora le temperature. Ma quan.short: I still measure temperatures. But when the wind brings the smell of burning peat, I cannot sleep. I think of those sleeping down there, who did not wake in time.

La notte del fuoco {0} non scese in paes.easy: On the night of the fire {0} did not go down to the village. They stayed in the tower all night, at the window, watching the smoke until dawn, with cold hands on the glass. The next morning they had breakfast with us, as always, and asked for the salt. We have never talked about that night again.
La notte del fuoco {0} non scese in paes.short: On the night of the fire {0} watched the smoke from the tower until dawn, cold hands on the glass. At breakfast they asked for the salt. We have never spoken of that night.

Il vecchio Fokke, quello svegliato dalla.easy: Old Fokke, the one they woke from the peat, had already been dead for three years. Hendrik says he would have been happy about it. He has never said so in front of his father.
Il vecchio Fokke, quello svegliato dalla.short: Old Fokke, woken from the peat, had died three years before. He would have been glad, says Hendrik. Never in front of his father.

Non c'è stato bisogno di votare. Quando.easy: We did not need to vote. When we came down from the tower at dawn, the village was awake. The whole village was waiting for us under the windows of the estate, in silence, with their hands in their pockets. They did not want anything. They only wanted us to know.
Non c'è stato bisogno di votare. Quando.short: No vote was needed. At dawn the whole village stood silent under the estate's windows, hands in pockets. They wanted nothing. Only for us to know.

Ho rifatto i conti del Registro. A {0} s.easy: I have done the sums of the Register again. There are only a few of us left in {0}: the family of the estate, Trijntje Kalf, Miss Borg, Hendrik Tammer, me, and a few stubborn old people who only drink gin. All the others are them. The mayor, the councillors, the teachers, the schoolchildren, the soldiers from the memorial. The village belongs to them, and it has for longer than we want to say. We are the last ones.
Ho rifatto i conti del Registro. A {0} s.short: I have redone the sums. We are few: the estate, Trijntje, Miss Borg, Hendrik, me, and a few old gin-drinkers. Everyone else is them, and has been for longer than we admit. We are the last.

Non ci fanno del male. Non ce ne hanno m.easy: They do not hurt us. They never have. They bring us fruit, repair our roofs, say hello to us by name, and wait. They have time: they always had more time than us. One by one, because we are tired, because we are lonely, because in the end sleep is sweet, we will drink too.
Non ci fanno del male. Non ce ne hanno m.short: They do us no harm. They bring fruit, mend our roofs, and wait. They have time. One by one, from tiredness, from loneliness, because sleep is sweet, we too will drink.

Stamattina, al risveglio, mi sono misura.easy: This morning, when I woke up, I took my temperature as I do every day. Thirty-five point nine. I put the thermometer back in its box and wrote the number here, with no comment. My father measured. My grandmother counted. From today, I wait.
Stamattina, al risveglio, mi sono misura.short: This morning: thirty-five point nine. I wrote it here without comment. My father measured. My grandmother counted. From today, I wait.

Alla tenuta, {0} ci tratta con una dolce.easy: At the estate, {0} is endlessly gentle with us. They bring us breakfast in bed, repair the shutters, and read to us in the evening when we cannot sleep. They have never asked us to drink. They know they do not need to: they only have to wait.
Alla tenuta, {0} ci tratta con una dolce.short: At the estate {0} is endlessly gentle: breakfast in bed, mended shutters, reading to us at night. They never ask us to drink. They need only wait.

La medaglia del consiglio, nell'ingresso.easy: The council's medal, in the entrance hall, shines more than ever. The mayor comes to polish it himself once a month, and every time he stays for dinner.
La medaglia del consiglio, nell'ingresso.short: The council's medal shines as never before. The mayor polishes it himself each month, and stays to dinner.

Siamo rimasti alla finestra della torre.easy: We stayed at the window of the tower until dawn, watching the bog. At the place where the light was, the snow still did not stay. At about seven the water moved. Slowly, with water up to the knees, a person we knew walked out of it: {0}, the real one, who had been sleeping under the peat since the night of the party. White skin, purple lips, teeth chattering.
Siamo rimasti alla finestra della torre.short: At dawn, from the tower, we watched the water move at the place of the light. Out of it, knee-deep, came {0}: the real one, asleep under the peat since the party. White, purple-lipped, teeth chattering.

Abbiamo portato {0} a casa, nelle copert.easy: We took {0} home in blankets and sat by the fire. I took the temperature every hour: thirty-four. Then thirty-five. Then, at midday, thirty-six point eight. Then the tears came, without a reason.
Abbiamo portato {0} a casa, nelle copert.short: By the fire, wrapped in blankets: thirty-four, thirty-five, and at noon thirty-six point eight. Then {0} wept, for no reason.

Delle ultime settimane non resta niente:.easy: Nothing is left of the last weeks: the party, the days at home, the evenings with the family, the test. Only a very long dream is left, where someone with the same face did everything better. It was not unpleasant, they say. Down there, there was only a great tiredness.
Delle ultime settimane non resta niente:.short: The last weeks are gone. Only a long dream remains, where someone with the same face did everything better. Not unpleasant, they say. Just a great tiredness.

Il paese, il giorno dopo, è venuto alla.easy: The next day the village came to the estate in silence, with flowers. Not for the person who came back, but for the other one. They left the flowers on the dyke, at the place where the light was, and went home.
Il paese, il giorno dopo, è venuto alla.short: Next day the village came with flowers. Not for the one who returned: for the other. They left them at the place of the light.

L'altro, laggiù, adesso dorme. Ha preso.easy: The other one, down there, is sleeping now. It has taken the place of the person it gave back. At least this sum adds up.
L'altro, laggiù, adesso dorme. Ha preso.short: The other sleeps down there now, in the place of the one it gave back. This sum, at least, adds up.

La pietra è rimasta alla tenuta, nella s.easy: The stone is still at the estate, warm, in its felt box. Since then nobody has been brave enough to decide what to do with it. Sometimes, at night, the person who came back from the bog goes down to the laboratory and puts a hand on it for a long time. They say that this is how they remember the dream.
La pietra è rimasta alla tenuta, nella s.short: The stone stays warm in its box. Nobody dares decide its fate. Some nights the one who returned rests a hand on it for a long time, to remember the dream.

La pietra è rimasta nella torbiera, nel.easy: The stone is still in the bog, at the place where the light was. Every Sunday at dawn, the person who came back goes there and stands on the dyke, looking at the water. They say they do not miss it. They say they only want to remember how it felt to be at peace.
La pietra è rimasta nella torbiera, nel.short: The stone stays in the bog. Every Sunday at dawn the one who returned stands on the dyke watching the water, not homesick, they say: only remembering peace.

Il martello di Jaap Mol è passato di man.easy: Jaap Mol's hammer went from hand to hand, and in the end someone lifted it. One exact blow, like Jaap's. The stone did not break into pieces: it opened like a fruit, and it was empty inside. The room filled with the smell of the bog, and then there was nothing. For the first time, the stone was cold.
Il martello di Jaap Mol è passato di man.short: One precise blow of Jaap Mol's hammer. The stone opened like a fruit, empty inside. A smell of bog, then nothing. For the first time, it was cold.

All'alba sono scesa in paese con la bors.easy: At dawn I went down to the village with my doctor's bag. It was no use. In every house, in the beds, on the chairs, behind the shop counters, there were piles of black, wet peat, with clothes, glasses, false teeth and wedding rings inside. Mayor Bram Wessel at his desk in the Town Hall. The bank cashier. The librarian. The three boys from the memorial. Everyone who had drunk, everyone who had come back from the bog a little different, from fifty years ago or from yesterday.
All'alba sono scesa in paese con la bors.short: At dawn my doctor's bag was useless. In beds, on chairs, behind counters: heaps of wet black peat, with clothes, spectacles, wedding rings. The mayor at his desk. The cashier. The librarian. The three boys. All who had drunk, all who had come back changed.

E alla tenuta, nella camera di {0}, sul.easy: And at the estate, in {0}'s room, on the pillow, there was a pile of peat shaped like a sleeping head.
E alla tenuta, nella camera di {0}, sul.short: And in {0}'s room, on the pillow, peat in the shape of a sleeping head.

{0} è un paese di vecchi, di bambini pic.easy: {0} is a village of old people, small children and empty houses. I have counted the living: one hundred and twenty. Before there were nine hundred. There is no council now. The school is closed, and so is the bank. At the market people argue again about the price of herring. At the inn they sing out of tune. Last night there was a fight. I fixed two broken noses, and I laughed the whole time.
{0} è un paese di vecchi, di bambini pic.short: One hundred and twenty living, out of nine hundred. No council, no school, no bank. At the market they quarrel over herring again; at the inn they sing out of tune. Last night I set two broken noses, laughing all the while.

Sotto la torba, nella torbiera, i dormie.easy: Under the peat, in the bog, the sleepers are still sleeping. Without the stone, we do not know if they will ever wake up. Gerrit Tammer, who is over sixty, goes there every morning with his spade and digs. He says that one day one of them will open their eyes.
Sotto la torba, nella torbiera, i dormie.short: The sleepers still sleep. Without the stone, perhaps for ever. Gerrit Tammer, past sixty, digs every morning. One of them, he says, will open their eyes.

La Macchina, nella torre, ronza ancora,.easy: The Machine in the tower still hums softly, every night at a quarter past eleven. We are not brave enough to turn it off. We do not know what it is waiting for.
La Macchina, nella torre, ronza ancora,.short: Every night at a quarter past eleven, the Machine still hums. We dare not switch it off. We do not know what it waits for.

Abbiamo scavato per un mese, con la vang.easy: We dug for a month, with Gerrit's spade and two hundred other spades. At the start there were only a few of us: the estate, the Watch, Hendrik. Then the Neighbours came too, though nobody called them, with spades on their shoulders and their sleeves rolled up. They dug next to us in silence and never got tired. They knew where to dig.
Abbiamo scavato per un mese, con la vang.short: We dug for a month. At first only the estate, the Watch and Hendrik. Then the Neighbours came, uncalled, with their spades, and dug beside us in silence, tireless. They knew where.

Li abbiamo tirati fuori a centinaia: bia.easy: We took them out by the hundred: white, cold, asleep, in clothes from fifty years ago, thirty years ago, last week. The miller's wife. Mrs Wessel, the mayor's mother. Mrs Mulder, whose husband thought she was with him in Rotterdam. They all woke up slowly, over a few days, in the school gym, which became a hospital. They lay under blankets, and Trijntje Kalf and I took their temperatures.
Li abbiamo tirati fuori a centinaia: bia.short: We brought them out by the hundred, cold and asleep, in the clothes of fifty years ago or last week: the miller's wife, Mrs Wessel, Mrs Mulder. They woke within days in the school gym, while Trijntje and I took temperatures.

Per primo, Fokke Tammer, giovane come ne.easy: The first was Fokke Tammer, as young as in 1865, with the burns on his palms. Gerrit stayed by him for three days.
Per primo, Fokke Tammer, giovane come ne.short: First came Fokke Tammer, young as in 1865, his palms burnt. Gerrit watched over him for three days.

Ora {0} ha due di tutti. Due Jan Hoek, d.easy: Now {0} has two of everyone. Two Jan Hoeks, two Piet Brinks, two miller's wives, who do not look at each other and do not talk. The people who woke up are tired, confused, angry and frightened. They do not know what year it is, they do not recognise the streets, and they cry for the children who grew up without them. The Neighbours help them with everything, with endless patience, like you help a sick relative. Nobody knows any more whose family is whose.
Ora {0} ha due di tutti. Due Jan Hoek, d.short: Now {0} has two of everyone, who never look at each other. The awakened are lost, angry, weeping for children grown without them. The Neighbours help them with infinite patience. Nobody can tell whose family is whose.

Nessuno sa che cosa succederà. Io so sol.easy: Nobody knows what will happen. I only know that last night, at the inn, a man who had just woken up hit his double. The double did not fight back. He hugged him. They stayed like that for a long time, one warm and one cold. Then they ordered two gins.
Nessuno sa che cosa succederà. Io so sol.short: Nobody knows what will come. Last night at the inn a man just woken punched his double, who embraced him. They stood a long time like that, one warm, one cold. Then they ordered two gins.

Anche alla tenuta, adesso, ci sono due {.easy: At the estate too there are two of {0} now. One came out of the peat remembering nothing after the night of the party. The other gave up the bedroom, the clothes and the chair at the table, and now sleeps on the sofa. They argue about everything. Every day they look less alike. This morning, for the first time, the one on the sofa sang a wrong note, and laughed.
Anche alla tenuta, adesso, ci sono due {.short: At the estate there are two of {0} now. One remembers nothing after the party; the other sleeps on the sofa. They argue about everything, and look less alike each day. This morning the one on the sofa sang a wrong note, and laughed.

La pietra è ancora alla tenuta, calda, n.easy: The stone is still at the estate, warm, in its box. The people who woke up do not want to go near the laboratory. Sometimes the Neighbours walk past it and stop for a moment, the way you stop in front of a church.
La pietra è ancora alla tenuta, calda, n.short: The warm stone stays in its box. The awakened shun the laboratory. The Neighbours pause before it, as before a church.

{0} ha messo la pietra sulla piattaforma.easy: {0} put the stone on the platform, in the middle of the ring. It was warm, and it was pulsing softly. The great-grandfather wrote it: *it must go back where it came from*. We did it. At a quarter past eleven the Machine turned on: white light, no heat, a hum like bees inside a wall. The stone disappeared.
{0} ha messo la pietra sulla piattaforma.short: {0} set the warm, pulsing stone on the platform. *It must go back where it came from.* At a quarter past eleven: white light, a hum of bees. The stone was gone.

Ho tirato fuori il Registro e l'ho apert.easy: I took out the Register and opened it at the first page, grandmother Hester's page. *11 November 1865. Night, a quarter past eleven. I saw a white light on the tower of the estate, as bright as day. At the same moment, another light just like it in the middle of the bog.* I looked out of the window, at the bog. There was nothing to see. There should not be: that light came on fifty-four years ago.
Ho tirato fuori il Registro e l'ho apert.short: I opened the Register at Hester's first page: *11 November 1865, a quarter past eleven. A white light on the tower; at the same instant, another in the bog.* I looked at the bog. Nothing. Of course: that light came on fifty-four years ago.

Il bisnonno pensava che qualcosa fosse p.easy: The great-grandfather thought that something came through from the other side and had to go back where it came from. He was wrong only about the direction. The stone did not come from another world, and he did not bring it here. We sent it. Tonight, trying to free the village from the stone, we sent it to the place where everything began. {0} became what it is because we, fifty-four years later, would send the stone back. The stone is in the past because it was in the future, and it is in the future because it was in the past. It does not come from anywhere. It goes round and round in a circle. And we are the point where the circle closes.
Il bisnonno pensava che qualcosa fosse p.short: Great-grandfather was wrong only about the direction. Nobody fetched the stone: we sent it. Trying to free {0}, we sent it to where it all began. It exists in the past because it existed in the future, and the other way round. It comes from nowhere. It goes in a circle, and we are where the circle closes.

Non nasceranno più Vicini. Quelli che ci.easy: No new Neighbours will be born. The ones who are here will stay as long as the peat lasts: ten years, twenty, fifty. They will fall apart one at a time, slowly, like Fokke. The village will have time to say goodbye to them. This morning at the market one of them asked me how I was, and for the first time there was something like fear in its voice.
Non nasceranno più Vicini. Quelli che ci.short: No more Neighbours will come. Those here will last as long as the peat: ten years, fifty. The village will have time to say goodbye. This morning one asked how I was, and for the first time its voice held something like fear.

Sul tavolo della torre ho lasciato l'oro.easy: I left my grandmother's watch on the table in the tower, stopped at a quarter past eleven. Now I know what time it shows.
Sul tavolo della torre ho lasciato l'oro.short: I left Hester's watch on the tower table, at a quarter past eleven. Now I know what time it shows.

{0} era nella stanza, quando la pietra è.easy: {0} was in the room when the stone disappeared. They looked at the empty platform for a long time, with their cold hands by their sides. Then they looked at each of us and said only: "Thank you. Now I know how much time I have." There was no anger in their voice. For the first time there was something like hurry.
{0} era nella stanza, quando la pietra è.short: {0} watched the empty platform a long time, cold hands at their sides. Then: "Thank you. Now I know how much time I have." No bitterness. For the first time, something like haste.

Il Morning Liberal, che a novembre aveva.easy: The Morning Liberal, which printed our statement in November, printed this one too. Under it, in small letters, the editor wrote: *If it is true, it is the saddest story I have ever printed. If it is not true, it still is.*
Il Morning Liberal, che a novembre aveva.short: The Morning Liberal printed this too, with the editor's note: *If it is true, it is the saddest story I have ever printed. If not, it still is.*

Abbiamo portato la pietra all'argine all.easy: At dawn we carried the stone to the dyke in the snow, wrapped in its sack. The whole village was waiting for us. Nobody spoke. When we gave it to them, they passed it from hand to hand, very carefully, down to the bank. Mayor Bram Wessel walked into the water up to his chest and put it down at the place where the light was. The stone sank without a sound. At last the snow began to stay on the ground.
Abbiamo portato la pietra all'argine all.short: At dawn the silent village passed the stone hand to hand to the bank, and Mayor Bram Wessel waded chest-deep to lay it at the place of the light. It sank without a sound. At last, the snow began to settle.

Da quel giorno i Vicini non si sbriciola.easy: From that day the Neighbours do not fall apart any more. The oldest ones, who had started to dry, got better in a week: the cracks closed and their skin was smooth again. They thanked us one by one, coming to the estate with flowers. They told us they will never forget it. I believe them: they never forget anything.
Da quel giorno i Vicini non si sbriciola.short: The Neighbours crumble no more. The oldest healed within a week. They came with flowers to thank us, and said they will never forget. I believe them: they never forget anything.

E la torbiera ricomincia. La fontana del.easy: And the bog starts again. The fountain in the square gives dark water again, fresh and good. The babies born this year drink it from their bottles. The council already has a plan for a long water pipe, to take {0} Water to the whole province, then to the whole kingdom, and then who knows where.
E la torbiera ricomincia. La fontana del.short: The bog begins again. Dark water flows from the fountain; this year's babies drink it from the bottle. The council plans an aqueduct: the province, the kingdom, and then who knows.

Ho deciso di restare. Qualcuno deve cont.easy: I have decided to stay. Someone must count. But last night, for the first time in my life, I drank a glass of water from the fountain. I wanted to know how peace tastes. It is good. Tomorrow morning I will take my temperature and write it here, as always. If I do not write it, you will know why.
Ho deciso di restare. Qualcuno deve cont.short: I will stay: someone must count. But last night I drank from the fountain, to taste peace. It is good. Tomorrow I will write my temperature here. If I do not, you will know why.

{0} mi ha accompagnata alla fontana, ier.easy: Last night {0} came with me to the fountain. They held the glass for me, kindly, like you do for a child taking medicine. They said I will not be sorry. They said that nobody in {1} has ever been sorry about anything.
{0} mi ha accompagnata alla fontana, ier.short: {0} came with me to the fountain and held the glass, as for a child taking medicine. I will not regret it, they said. Nobody in {1} ever regrets anything.

La Macchina, nella torre, è rimasta acce.easy: The Machine in the tower stayed on for three days after the night of the vote, humming, with nothing on the platform. Then it turned itself off. Since then nobody has tried to turn it on.
La Macchina, nella torre, è rimasta acce.short: The Machine hummed for three days over its empty platform, then switched itself off. Nobody has tried it since.

Abbiamo votato di non fare niente. È una.easy: We voted to do nothing. That is a choice too, the most common choice of all. The stone stays in the bog, the sleepers sleep, the Neighbours say hello to us in the street. The village is quiet. Tomorrow it will be as quiet as today, and the day after it will be even quieter.
Abbiamo votato di non fare niente. È una.short: We voted to do nothing: the commonest choice of all. The stone stays, the sleepers sleep, the Neighbours greet us. Tomorrow will be as quiet as today, and the day after, quieter.

Chiudo il Registro qui. Tre generazioni.easy: I am closing the Register here. Three generations of temperatures, cold hands and names with a small cross next to them. My grandmother counted them, my father measured them, and I added them up. The total is useless if nobody reads it. I leave it to the family of the estate. They can keep it in the tower, next to the Machine that was no use and the watch that does not tell the time any more.
Chiudo il Registro qui. Tre generazioni.short: I close the Register: three generations of temperatures and crosses. Grandmother counted, father measured, I added up. A total is useless unread. I leave it in the tower, beside the useless Machine and the stopped watch.

Ogni tanto, la sera, vado sull'argine a.easy: Sometimes, in the evening, I go to the dyke to look at the bog. At the place where the light was, the snow never stays. Below, hundreds of sleepers go on sleeping, with their hands together, kept just as they were on the day they were taken. Above, the ones who walk go on walking: kind, healthy, at peace. In fifty years they will fall apart, others will take their place, and nobody in {0} will notice.
Ogni tanto, la sera, vado sull'argine a.short: Some evenings I watch the bog from the dyke. Below, hundreds sleep on, preserved. Above, the others walk on, kind and at peace. In fifty years others will take their place, and nobody will notice.

Non so se abbiamo sbagliato. Ma per la p.easy: I do not know if we made a mistake. But for the first time in my life, as I close this notebook, I feel quiet too. And that frightens me more than anything else.
Non so se abbiamo sbagliato. Ma per la p.short: I do not know if we were wrong. But closing this notebook, I feel quiet too. That frightens me most of all.

{0}, dopo il voto, mi ha accompagnata a.easy: After the vote {0} walked me home in the snow, holding the umbrella for me. At the door they thanked me. For what? "For leaving things as they are," they said. "It is the kindest thing you can do."
{0}, dopo il voto, mi ha accompagnata a.short: {0} walked me home under an umbrella and thanked me at the door, "for leaving things as they are. It is the kindest thing one can do."

La famiglia della tenuta, almeno, non ha.easy: At least the family of the estate never accepted the medal. It is not much. But in {0} now, not much is all we have left that is ours.
La famiglia della tenuta, almeno, non ha.short: At least the estate never took the medal. It is little. But little is all that is still ours.

Le mani fredde, nel Registro, sono quara.easy: There are forty-one cold hands in the Register now. I do not tell the council any more.
Le mani fredde, nel Registro, sono quara.short: Forty-one cold hands in the Register. I no longer tell the council.

\"Non è lui\", dice la vedova. \"Lo so c.easy: "It is not him," says the widow. "I know it is him. But it is not him."
\"Non è lui\", dice la vedova. \"Lo so c.short: "I know it is him," says the widow. "But it is not him."

Sul tavolo c'è la vecchia lanterna della.easy: On the table there is the old lantern of the first watch, the pastor's lantern. Someone kept it.
Sul tavolo c'è la vecchia lanterna della.short: On the table: the pastor's old lantern from the first watch. Someone kept it.

La medaglia del consiglio è appesa nell'.easy: The council's medal hangs in the hall of the estate, next to the big clock. It shines. Nobody touches it.
La medaglia del consiglio è appesa nell'.short: The council's medal gleams in the hall. Nobody touches it.

Il consiglio manda ancora la cesta di fr.easy: The council still sends the basket of fruit every month. The fruit is perfect. At the estate they give it to the pigs.
Il consiglio manda ancora la cesta di fr.short: The council's perfect fruit still comes every month. The estate feeds it to the pigs.

Il cane della tenuta, un nipote di Bruin.easy: The estate's dog, one of Bruin's grandchildren, runs onto the ice barking, before anyone else moves.
Il cane della tenuta, un nipote di Bruin.short: Bruin's grandson is first onto the ice, barking.

Il certificato di {0} è già sul tavolo,.easy: {0}'s certificate has been on the table for days, turned over. All the others show the crown.
Il certificato di {0} è già sul tavolo,.short: {0}'s certificate has lain turned on the table for days. The rest show the crown.

La medaglia d'argento del consiglio è an.easy: The council's silver medal is still in the hall of the estate. It has never gone dark.
La medaglia d'argento del consiglio è an.short: The council's silver medal still hangs in the hall. It has never tarnished.

Jan Hoek, il suo fidanzato tornato dalle.easy: Jan Hoek, her fiancé who came back from Flanders, wrote her the same letter every week for fifty years.
Jan Hoek, il suo fidanzato tornato dalle.short: Jan Hoek wrote her the same letter every week for fifty years.

Gerrit, almeno, il suo l'ha già svegliat.easy: Gerrit has already woken his own father once. He says he knows how to do it.
Gerrit, almeno, il suo l'ha già svegliat.short: Gerrit has woken his father once already. He knows how.
